jobs.title: Dedicated Care Coordinator NY Metro
jobs.excerpt: Why Patients Need YouThe Inflammation and Immunology Dedicated Care Coordinator (DCC) is a non-promotional, field-based role that supports patients’ access to PDPA and VFM products when prescribed by a licensed healthcare provider.
jobs.description:
Why Patients Need You

The Inflammation and Immunology Dedicated Care Coordinator (DCC) is a non-promotional, field-based role that supports patients’ access to PDPA and VFM products when prescribed by a licensed healthcare provider. The DCC owns the continual management and progression of the patient journey — from HUB enrollment through post-fill follow-up — working directly with patients, providers, payers, HUB partners, and third-party vendors. It is a dual patient- and HCP-facing role spanning a patient journey, and the colleague in this role carries 100% ownership of every case in their assigned geography.

What You Will Achieve

The DCC is a subject-matter expert on reimbursement, access, and coverage issues that can educate patients/caregivers and healthcare providers on matters relating to reimbursement, access, and coverage. The DCC will serve as the primary point of contact for patients/caregivers and healthcare providers regarding the status of their request for reimbursement support and access assistance and will also provide updates to patients/caregivers and healthcare providers on their status as appropriate. The DCC holds end-to-end case ownership: benefits investigation and verification, prior authorization and appeals support, appointment and baseline assessment coordination, Interim Care and voucher administration, copay support, prescription triage, and scheduled post-fill follow-up.

How You Will Achieve It

Case Ownership and the Patient Journey

  • Own 100% of assigned cases and drive the continual management and progression of the patient journey, from HUB enrollment through post-fill follow-up

  • Be the central point-of-contact for patients/caregivers and HCP providers regarding the status of their request for reimbursement and access support related to a patient case.

  • Answer questions from patients/caregivers relating to access and coverage

  • Maintain a clear understanding of the patient access journey and requirements at each stage of the process, as well as the role played by patients/caregivers and HCP providers in the process

  • Support access with HCPs and opted-in patients/caregivers who have been prescribed a PDPA OR VFM product

Benefits Investigation and Financial Navigation

  • Conduct the Summary of Benefits (SOB) discussion required for every HUB-enrolled patient, reviewing both the product benefit structure, any associated cost and the baseline appointments for VFM

  • Obtain all missing information on the Patient Enrollment Form (PEF) and verify the testing, voucher, and Interim Care options selected by the HCP office

  • Walk the patient through out-of-pocket cost, deductibles, copay options, and the reimbursement program, including the impact of maximizers and accumulators

  • Verify coverage for the product and for required baseline tests across both PBM and major medical insurance for VFM

  • Oversee the entire prior authorization process, including submission and verification with both the patient and the provider

  • Conduct benefit investigation and verification (BI/BV) calls directly with payers and patients for patients with 3rd party restrictions

  • Confirm and communicate product coverage, cost, prior authorization and appeal requirements, Interim Care program PA and Appeal deadlines, and baseline assessment tests to HCP and patient

Appointment and Assessment Coordination

  • Schedule, reschedule and confirm patient appointments in coordination with the patient, the provider, and the vendor

  • Secure the appropriate confirmation communication back from the provider (CFT)

  • Coordinate compliantly with IQVIA/MDX on patient assessment tests — confirm tests are completed and reschedule where needed

Program and Copay Administration

  • Once IC is approved, manage all Interim Care (IC) program administrative requirements and deadlines with the provider and the patient, including Extended Interim Care programs

  • Confirm voucher need and eligibility with the provider and patient, and triage the voucher for shipment to the patient

  • Maintain Copay portal access and help approved commercial patients secure a copay card

  • Own copay eligibility attestation responsibility

  • Follow up with the patient post-fill to confirm the copay card is functioning correctly

Prescription Triage, Fulfillment, and Ongoing Follow-Up

  • Triage the voucher, paid prescription, and/or Interim Care fill within Polaris

  • Contact the patient at 10 days and again at 45 days post-prescription, confirming that no logistical or financial questions remain outstanding

Case and Systems Ownership

  • Manage and update various case types in Polaris, using its texting, faxing, and prescription triage capabilities

  • View and interpret prior authorization, appeal, and PEF documentation for accuracy

  • Share and manage cases with HUB partners across all patient journeys

  • Coordinate as appropriate with other Pfizer colleagues and Patient Support Program/HUB employees, via tasks and secure messages to requests for action, to help resolve problems with individual patient cases

  • Maintain case comments as a real-time account of the patient journey, including a recap of every call made to the HCP and the patient

  • Use the Kite works encrypted email system for correspondence with patients and providers

  • Manage the Docusign process with patients to obtain required consents

  • Develop an organized, concise, and compliant way to manage assigned patient cases within established time frames

Compliance, Safety Reporting, and Communication

  • Report adverse events (AEs) in accordance with company requirements — AE reporting volume is elevated in this role, patient contact is more frequent and spans the entire patient journey

  • Operate within the tighter content controls and system permissions that apply to this role

  • Compliantly communicate the access landscape and options to patients/caregivers and HCPs

  • Link the patient access support to meet patient needs, using Brand RC-approved materials

  • Conduct yourself with the utmost discretion and confidentiality

  • Adhere to strict company compliance guidelines and procedures

  • Work and lead cross-functionally with internal and external colleagues, compliantly, to improve the patient access journey

  • Effectively link customer insights to the offerings and approved resources to address patient access barriers

  • Build trust through compliant follow-up and knowledge of the access journey

  • Demonstrate excellence in responsible business communication, both written and spoken

Qualifications

Must-Have

  • B.S. or B.A. Degree 8+ years of pharmaceutical (or related) experience in customer-facing roles/functions.

  • 6 months minimum as a FRM, PAC, FAS or similar experience in access and Reimbursement and working with Polaris CRM System.

  • Working proficiency in Polaris, including case management and documentation, prescription triage, and interpretation of PA, appeal, and PEF documentation

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate directly with patients, with providers, and with cross-functional colleagues

  • Experience conducting benefit investigation and verification directly with payers, and working knowledge of prior authorization and appeals processes

  • Working knowledge of copay programs, copay maximizers and accumulators, vouchers, and free or interim care programs

  • Ability to own a high volume of concurrent cases across a patient journey that could average approximately 20 days, with disciplined documentation and follow-through

  • Ability to meet adverse event reporting obligations in a role with frequent, direct patient contact

  • Strong understanding of Reimbursement, Government Payment Systems, Specialty Pharmacy Networks, Co-Pay Assistance Programs, and knowledge of the Specialty Medication area.

  • Appropriate and compliant communication and collaboration with cross-functional field-based colleagues (Sales, Medical, FRM, PCA/SAS, KAD, Government Relations) to ensure optimal and appropriate patient access in both in-patient and out-patient accounts.

  • Alignment with HQ stakeholders to ensure appropriate understanding of, and support for patient access (e.g., Brand and Customer Marketing teams and PCA/SAS teams).

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience in a Patient and/or customer facing role requiring access and reimbursement education.

  • Experience working with a HUB.

  • Experience with Kite works or a comparable encrypted email platform, Docusign, and copay portal administration

  • Experience coordinating with third-party vendors on patient assessment, testing, or specialty pharmacy logistics (e.g., IQVIA/MDX, Sonexus)

  • Experience supporting Interim Care, free goods, or bridge programs

  • Experience with both pharmacy benefit (PBM) and major medical benefit coverage pathways

Knowledge & Skill Sets Desired:

  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

  • Exceptional relationship building skills, especially with elderly age groups

  • Trust

  • Integrity

  • Empathy

  • Patience

  • Deliver meaningful & concise presentations

  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills

  • Exceptional critical thinking skills, ability to understand complex processes and effectively communicate to diverse community of patients

  • Outstanding collaboration and networking abilities

  • Ability to work in a team environment

  • Understanding of Specialty Pharmaceuticals and Patient Journeys

  • Adherence to Regulatory and Compliance Standards

  • Flexibility to work across different time zones if needed

Other Job Details

  • Work Location Assignment: Remote colleagues from home 5 days a week or are field-based colleagues that are not affiliated with a Pfizer site.

  • Ability to travel – Approximately 10% to 20%

  • Time Zone: Eastern time zone.

  • Eligible for Relocation Package – NO

  • LAST DAY TO APPLY - 9/18/2026

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $162,900.00 to $271,500.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States.This role is posted in multiple locations. jobs.description:
Location Designation: Hybrid - 3 days per quarter

Business Unit

Technology, Data, AI and Ventures (TDAV)

Business Unit Overview

Within the Tech, Data, AI, Ventures (TDAV) organization, our work is guided by a shared vision: deploying the power of technology, data, AI and ventures to accelerate sustainable competitive advantage for New York Life's businesses. We build solutions that power how we serve policy owners, agents, advisors and employees while delivering measurable business outcomes.

Across technology, data, AI, cyber, product, digital experience, architecture and infrastructure, TDAV combines the scale and investment of an industry leader, access to leading-edge technologies and the opportunity to help shape how a world-class financial services company competes in the AI era — all backed by the stability and purpose of a mutual company built to last.

Role Overview

The Cyber Security Operations team is seeking a Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst to help protect New York Life's enterprise technology environment by monitoring, detecting, investigating, and responding to cyber threats across hybrid and cloud environments. This role combines hands-on incident response, cloud security operations, and threat detection to identify and mitigate evolving cyber risks while strengthening the organization's overall security posture.

As a member of the Security Operations Center, you will leverage SIEM, EDR/XDR, cloud-native security technologies, and threat intelligence to investigate security events, conduct threat hunting, and coordinate incident response activities. You will collaborate with security engineering, cloud platform, infrastructure, and application teams to improve detection capabilities, automate response processes, and support a resilient, secure technology environment.

What You'll Do

  • Monitor, investigate, and respond to security alerts and incidents across cloud and on-premises environments using SIEM, EDR/XDR, and cloud-native security platforms, ensuring timely detection, containment, and resolution of cyber threats.

  • Perform threat hunting, malware analysis, and incident investigations involving phishing, ransomware, identity compromise, unauthorized access, and other advanced attack techniques while documenting findings and recommending remediation actions.

  • Analyze security telemetry and logs from cloud platforms, including AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and cloud security services, to identify indicators of compromise, emerging threats, and opportunities to strengthen security controls.

  • Develop and maintain incident response playbooks, standard operating procedures, and automation workflows while participating in tabletop exercises, security assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational readiness.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional technology and cybersecurity teams to improve cloud security posture, reduce operational risk, leverage AI-enabled security capabilities, and provide actionable reporting to technical and business stakeholders.

What You'll Bring

Required Skills

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience) with 3–4 years of experience in Security Operations, Incident Response, Cyber Defense, or a related cybersecurity discipline.

  • Hands-on experience securing cloud environments using Amazon Web Services (AWS) and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including familiarity with cloud-native security services such as AWS GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, or Google Security Command Center.

  • Experience working with SIEM platforms such as Elastic, Splunk, or Google Chronicle, along with EDR/XDR technologies including CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne, or Palo Alto Cortex XDR.

  • Strong understanding of incident response methodologies, threat detection, log analysis, cloud identity security, MITRE ATT&CK, Cyber Kill Chain, Zero Trust principles, and identity and access management (IAM).

  • Knowledge of networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, VPNs, firewalls, IDS/IPS, proxy technologies, and the ability to investigate cloud-based attacks, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.

  • Experience with scripting or automation using Python, PowerShell, or Bash, strong analytical and communication skills, and the ability to leverage AI-enabled tools to improve investigation quality and operational efficiency.

Preferred Skills

  • Industry certifications such as GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH), AWS Certified Security – Specialty, CompTIA Security+, CompTIA CySA+, or comparable cybersecurity certifications.

  • Experience supporting a 24x7 Security Operations Center (SOC), implementing SOAR automation, and developing security orchestration workflows.

  • Familiarity with container security, Kubernetes, Docker, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform or CloudFormation), and DevSecOps practices.

  • Understanding of AI agents, AI frameworks, AI security risks, and emerging cyber threats targeting AI-enabled applications and platforms.

Success Measures

  • Timely detection, investigation, and response to cybersecurity incidents.

  • Continuous reduction in Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Respond (MTTR).

  • Accurate and comprehensive incident documentation, reporting, and root cause analysis.

  • Ongoing improvement of cloud security posture and detection capabilities.

  • Effective collaboration across cybersecurity, cloud, infrastructure, and application teams to reduce enterprise cyber risk.

Pay Transparency

Salary Range: $100,000-$143,000

Overtime eligible: Exempt

Discretionary bonus eligible: Yes

Sales bonus eligible: No

Actual base salary will be determined based on several factors but not limited to individual’s experience, skills, qualifications, and job location. Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. In addition to base salary, employees may also be eligible to participate in an incentive program.

Company Overview

At New York Life, our 180-year legacy of purpose and integrity fuels our future. As we evolve into a more technology-, data-, and AI-enabled organization, we remain grounded in the values that drive lasting impact.

Our diverse business portfolio creates opportunities to make a difference across industries and communities—inviting bold thinking, collaborative problem-solving, and purpose-driven innovation. Here, you’ll find the rare balance of long-standing stability and forward momentum, supported by an inclusive team that honors tradition while embracing progress.

As a Fortune 100 mutual company, we offer a place to grow your skills, contribute to meaningful work, and deliver solutions that matter. Your ideas drive what’s next, and your growth powers it.

Our Benefits

We provide a full package of benefits for employees – and have unique offerings for a modern workforce, including leave programs, adoption assistance, and student loan repayment programs. Based on feedback from our employees, we continue to refine and add benefits to our offering, so that you can flourish both inside and outside of work.Click hereto discover more about our comprehensive benefit options or visit our NYL Benefits Site.

Our Commitment to Inclusion
At New York Life, fostering an inclusive workplace is fundamental to who we are and how we serve our communities. We have a longstanding commitment to creating an environment where individuals can contribute their best and succeed together. This foundation is rooted in our core values of humanity and integrity, ensuring that every employee feels valued and supported. By embracing a broad range of perspectives and experiences, we achieve greater success and fulfill our promise of providing financial security and peace of mind to families across all communities. *Please note that while this role will operate remotely, it is required that the candidate resides in the Western region of the United States. This includes candidates residing in Pacific or Mountain time zones. At this time we are not considering candidates in the Bay Area*

Do you love local businesses, and want to help them grow? The Yelp Customer Success team is seeking a dedicated and driven Inbound Sales Retention Specialist to provide a 5-star experience to our small business advertisers! As a member of the Inbound Sales Retention team, you will be committed to supporting, consulting, and retaining our advertisers post-sale. We’d love to have you apply, even if you don’t feel you meet every single requirement in this posting. At Yelp, we’re looking for great people, not just those who simply check off all the boxes.

What you'll do:

    • You will help strengthen Yelp’s revenue retention by providing exceptional and timely customer support

    • You will be logged into an inbound phone queue for the majority of your day, consulting and educating our current Yelp advertisers

    • You will show clients the value of Yelp by highlighting their investment returns through ad performance metrics

    • You will use strong listening and conflict resolution skills to handle escalated clients

    • You will become an expert in Yelp’s advertising solutions and adapt product recommendations quickly to suit client needs - asking probing questions and handling objections will be critical to your success

    • You will exhibit strong communication skills, both externally with clients and internally with other Yelp employees

    • You will remain organized and efficient in a fast-paced environment

    • You will consistently achieve/exceed monthly goals

    • Use Chatbench, Yelp’s internal tool that provides secure access to a number of LLM models, to research, draft proposals, analyze data and overcome objections

What it takes to succeed:

  • You have a Bachelor's Degree or 3+ years of relevant client facing experience
  • You are technically proficient with computers and information systems
  • You have strong communication skills (verbal and written)
  • You excel with problem solving and troubleshooting
  • You have experience in account management, sales, advertising, or small business (preferred)
  • You have a love for local businesses and understand their importance in local economies
  • You have excellent time management and organizational skills with the ability to track and complete numerous details
  • You have the ability to handle tough conversations with business owners in a professional, solutions-oriented manner
  • You have the ability to strike a balance between consulting and supporting as needed
  • You are willing to receive and implement feedback
  • You have the ability to embrace a fast paced and always-changing environment
  • You will need access to an individual hardline high-speed internet connection in your workspace. This job cannot be performed using satellite internet or a mobile hotspot

What you'll get:

  • Effective your first day: Medical, vision, and dental
  • Mental health support and services via Modern Health
  • 15 days PTO (accrual begins on date of hire and increases with 2+ years of tenure thereafter), 12 paid holidays, plus one floating holiday and 7 paid wellness days

  • Monthly wellness subsidy
  • Flexible spending account
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan
  • Employee stock purchase plan
  • Work from home reimbursement
  • The base salary is $50,000 + performance based incentives

jobs.excerpt: Dentons Business Services EMEA is the operational backbone of Dentons, supporting the world's largest law firm in delivering exceptional service to clients across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.
jobs.description:
Dentons Business Services EMEA is the operational backbone of Dentons, supporting the world's largest law firm in delivering exceptional service to clients across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. As a crucial component of Dentons' global network, our EMEA business services team plays a key role in driving efficiency, innovation, and collaboration.

At Dentons Business Services EMEA, we are committed to excellence in supporting legal professionals with cutting-edge solutions. Our dynamic and diverse team collaborates seamlessly to provide a wide range of services, including finance, IT, human resources, marketing, and more. We pride ourselves on fostering a culture of continuous improvement and adaptability.

Job Purpose

The Senior Legal Engineer plays a key role within the Legal Tech Enablement team, designing and implementing legal technology solutions that improve service delivery across Dentons Europe. The role combines technical expertise with legal process knowledge to deliver automation, workflow optimisation, and innovative tools for lawyers and clients. This is an opportunity to play a visible role in shaping how legal services are delivered across a leading international law firm. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of law, technology, and innovation, leading meaningful change, delivering practical solutions, and helping scale legal tech capability across multiple jurisdictions.

Senior Legal Engineers lead legal engineering projects from concept to deployment, collaborate closely with practice groups to understand requirements, and mentor Legal Engineers and Junior Legal Engineers. They act as subject matter experts and contribute to the strategic direction of legal technology initiatives.

Responsibilities include developing automation solutions, implementing legal technology platforms, improving legal workflows, building custom applications and integrations, and managing relationships with selected technology vendors. The role also involves stakeholder engagement, solution design, user training, and ensuring the quality and scalability of deployed systems.

Some positions may also involve specialised responsibilities in eDiscovery and litigation support.

This role offers opportunities to develop leadership capabilities, deepen expertise in legal technologies, and contribute to the firm’s innovation strategy.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead end-to-end delivery of legal engineering projects (automation, document assembly, data extraction, custom applications).
  • Analyse legal workflows with practice groups and design technology solutions to optimise processes.
  • Build and configure solutions using automation and low-code/no-code platforms.
  • Prepare technical specifications, implementation plans, and documentation.
  • Test, troubleshoot, and maintain deployed solutions.
  • Work closely with partners, lawyers, Technology, and Business Development teams to deliver solutions.
  • Act as the main point of contact for vendors, managing implementations and training.
  • Present solution designs, run user testing, and support adoption across teams.
  • Contribute to the legal technology roadmap and evaluate new tools.
  • Support business cases, ROI analysis, and proof-of-concept initiatives.
  • Identify opportunities to scale successful solutions across practice areas.
  • Mentor and guide Legal Engineers and Junior Legal Engineers.
  • Foster collaboration and knowledge sharing across the team.
  • Maintain documentation, monitor solution performance, and implement improvements.
  • Stay up to date with legal tech developments and share insights with the team.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Law, Computer Science, Engineering, Social Sciences, or a related field.
  • Advanced degree or certifications in legal tech, innovation, or technology (preferred).
  • 4+ years of experience in legal technology, legal engineering, legal operations, software development, or a related field in delivering legal tech solutions from concept to deployment.
  • Hands-on experience with workflow automation, document automation, or legal applications.
  • Experience mentoring junior team members or working in client-facing/consulting roles is a plus.
  • Strong understanding of legal workflows and service delivery. Ability to assess technical feasibility while keeping user experience and business value in focus.
  • Experience with legal technology platforms (e.g., document automation, workflow tools, legal AI).
  • Familiarity with process mapping, software development lifecycle, and testing practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Lead change management efforts to ensure new tools and workflows are embedded successfully across teamsExcellent communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. Ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams and influence stakeholders. Build trusted relationships with partners and senior stakeholders to identify opportunities and drive adoption of legal technology solutions.
  • Highly organised, proactive, and comfortable working in dynamic environments.
  • Mentorship mindset with a collaborative, client-focused approach.

Benefits

  • Remuneration and benefits package will reflect the successful candidates experience and country where hired.

About Edged Data Centers Edged is a fast-growing provider of sustainable data centers and energy infrastructure. The company builds and operates a global network of ultra-efficient, AI-ready data centers with waterless cooling for colocation, hyperscale and build-to-suit customers. The highly differentiated infrastructure platform is the first large-scale, global deployment of waterless cooling platform-wide and transforms data center growth into a catalyst for sustainable development. Edged is backed by a deep proprietary technology stack that will include renewable microgrid systems, ultra-clean generators, and waste-to-fuel solutions. The platform is designed for rapid deployment with more than a dozen new data centers operating or under construction across Europe and North America and a gigawatt-scale project pipeline. The North American division of Edged is a joint venture between one of the largest private multinational corporations in the world and an affiliate of Endeavour. Endeavour is a purpose-driven organization helping innovators to develop and launch breakthrough solutions for global challenges in the areas of energy, water, and waste. Endeavour companies are made up of passionate change-makers who want to leave the world better than the way we found it. Today, Endeavour is deploying solutions that are immediately scalable and deliver both high financial returns and positive impact, including EV charging, waterless data center cooling, and advanced energy systems.

Opportunity Reporting to the Treasurer, the Treasury Manager will assist in managing Edged’s treasury operations. This position will focus on debt and liquidity management, bank and investor relationships, all while partnering with various teams across the organization. Key Responsibilities

Include but are not limited to:

  • Debt Portfolio Management: Monitor debt portfolios, track financial covenants, and ensure compliance with all reporting requirements
  • Cash & Liquidity Management: Assist the Treasurer in maintaining optimal liquidity to meet funding needs across the EDC platform
  • Collaborate with finance & accounting and Project Delivery teams to prepare and maintain cash flow forecasts and budgets
  • Partner with the Corporate Development team on new debt financing negotiations, focusing on potential operational challenges in the debt facilities
  • Assist in managing monthly debt and equity capital calls
  • Assist in managing relationships with lenders and banking partners

Skills & Requirements Education / Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Engineering, or a related field
  • Experience in digital infrastructure and real estate project finance highly preferred
  • CTP and/or CFA designation (or progress toward) preferred
  • MBA, Master’s degree in Finance or Business, or equivalent professional experience preferred

Skills / Abilities

  • 5+ years of experience in finance or treasury management in a corporate or banking environment, with a strong background in corporate finance, external debt management and liquidity management
  • Experience in debt capital markets, strategic finance, investment management, and working knowledge of interest rate derivatives / hedging activities
  • Strong work ethic, self-motivated, resourceful and capable of effective independent judgement
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel and excellent presentation skills; experience with treasury management systems is a plus
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and within a team environment
  • High level of initiative, ownership, and attention to detail in a fast-moving environment

Hiring and employment decisions within Edged are not based on religion, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, or marital, veteran, or disability status. jobs.excerpt: About Us:Our purpose is to help clients exceed their financial health goals.
jobs.description:
About Us:

Our purpose is to help clients exceed their financial health goals. Across the reimbursement cycle, our scalable solutions and clinical expertise help solve programmatic needs. Enabling our teams with leading technology allows analytics to guide our solutions and keeps us accountable achieving goals.

We build long-term careers by investing in YOU. We seek to create an environment that cultivates your professional development and personal growth, as we believe your success is our success.

JOB SUMMARY:

The Supervisor, DRG Integrity Reviews/Audits, is responsible for overseeing the execution, quality, and delivery of complex, concurrent, and retrospective coding audits. This role ensures compliance with AHA, CMS, AMA, AHIMA, AAPC, Coding Clinic, CPT Assistant, and official coding guidelines, while supervising a team of auditors. The Supervisor provides second-level review, client deliverables, coding education, and quality assurance to support both client and organizational goals.

CCS through AHIMA is required

This is a remote position

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Note: The essential duties and responsibilities below are intended to describe the general duties and responsibilities of this position and are not intended to be an exhaustive statement of duties. This position may perform all or most of the primary duties listed below. Specific tasks, responsibilities or competencies may be documented in the Team Member’s performance objectives as outlined by the Team Member’s immediate Leadership Team Member.

Team Supervision & Leadership

  • Coordinate scheduling of team and client deliverables with leadership.
  • Assign new clients to auditors, send weekly assignments, and ensure access to client information.
  • Provide auditors with timely updates/changes to coding guidelines and department processes.
  • Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for auditors across assigned audits.
  • Conduct training for new and existing auditors to maintain team competency.
  • Provide insight to auditor performance; productivity, quality and opportunity find rates
  • Conduct QA of at least 25% of departmental work products, ensuring a minimum 95% accuracy threshold.
  • Promote teamwork, knowledge sharing, and respectful communication across the team.

Productivity & Quality Standards

  • Meet productivity standards set by record type for each audit.
  • Maintain billable productive hours at or above 80% when client work is available.
  • Monitor and report time, work products, and schedules in an accurate and timely manner.
  • Recommend process improvements to streamline workflows and enhance efficiency.

Education & Professional Development

  • Participate in development and delivery of coding education for clients.
  • Stay current on coding, reimbursement, and compliance issues through continuing education.
  • Maintain active professional credentials as required.

Audit & Compliance

  • Perform complex concurrent and/or retrospective analysis of medical record documentation to validate coded data.
  • Ensure compliance with legal and procedural policies, official coding guidelines, and AHIMA Standards of Ethical Coding.
  • Conduct independent QA on assigned Reviews/Audits results with a minimum accuracy expectation of 95%.
  • Protect the privacy and confidentiality of patient and client health information at all times.

Reporting & Client Deliverables

  • Analyze Reviews/Audits findings and identify root causes of coding errors.
  • Prepare detailed summary reports of findings, citing official references.
  • Ensure deliverables are accurate, timely, and aligned with client expectations.
  • Act as client liaison/expert in organizational policies, maintaining an audit playbook for each assigned client.
  • Provide back-up leadership support for client interactions when needed.

Special Projects

  • Lead or participate in special projects requiring coding and auditing expertise across the organization.
  • Support leadership in implementing new initiatives and process improvements.

Qualifications and Requirements:

  • CCS credential (through AHIMA) required.
  • Minimum 5 years’ experience in DRG auditing, coding, or HIM consulting.
  • Previous supervisory or lead auditor experience strongly preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of ICD-10-CM/PCS, CPT, MS-DRG, APR-DRG, and reimbursement methodologies.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and report-writing skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced consulting environment.

Performance Expectations

  • Audit QA accuracy threshold: 95% minimum.
  • Billable productivity threshold: 50% minimum (when client work is available).
  • Demonstrated ability to apply coding principles consistently to evolving scenarios.

This is a remote position

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:
Note: Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions as described. Regular eye-hand coordination and manual dexterity is required to operate office equipment. The ability to perform work at a computer terminal for 6-8 hours a day and function in an environment with constant interruptions is required. At times, Team Members are subject to sitting for prolonged periods. Infrequently, Team Member must be able to lift and move material weighing up to 20 lbs. Team Member may experience elevated levels of stress during periods of increased activity and with work entailing multiple deadlines.

In this role, you will specifically innovate on Internal Tools to improve our users' day-to-day experiences and build and maintain robust connections with external Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS). Engineering Manager (Remote)

Full-Time, Remote / Salary, Exempt / Includes Benefits, PTO, Flexible Schedule, Equity

At Steno, we’re growing fast and transforming the litigation technology industry with best-in-class court reporting, modern solutions that add value for lawyers, and an exceptional client experience. We partner with law firms to simplify complex workflows, deliver reliable outcomes and case insights, and to revolutionize a traditionally outdated space while we expand across the country.

Steno has experienced rapid growth and market adoption since its release in early 2019, and we are now ready to bring on additional engineering talent to help us build intelligent systems that meet our customers' evolving needs.

Who are you?

An amazing, AI-powered product begins with amazing people who are ready to upend a traditional industry. As a technical manager on a growing team, you will be instrumental in leading and developing a team of engineers while ensuring high technical standards and alignment with business objectives.

If you're passionate about leadership and technical excellence with strong software engineering and SDLC fundamentals, and an enthusiasm for our engineering culture of continuous improvement - come join us!

  • Participating in technical discussions and reviews to maintain high technical standards
  • Collaborating with other departments on cross-functional initiatives
  • Managing resource allocations and project planning
  • Providing technical guidance and mentorship to direct reports
  • Engaging in recruitment and interviewing processes to grow the team
  • Help triage, investigate root causes, and support critical system issues as they arise
  • Conducting regular one-on-ones with direct reports for performance monitoring and mentorship
  • Championing and continuously improving Steno's SDLC process
  • Facilitating communication regarding engineering-related compliance activities (SOC2, Penetration Testing, etc.)
  • Reviewing, managing, and approving employee expense submissions

  • You possess a track record of developing talented software teams
  • You have experience with multiple software project methodologies (Scrum, Kanban, etc.)
  • You understand compliance and security considerations in software development
  • You have experience in adapting processes and procedures in response to changing team and business needs
  • You're passionate about revolutionizing traditional industries through technology

This job may not be for you if:

  • You’d prefer not to “roll up your sleeves” when it comes to getting technical and solving problems
  • You're uncomfortable with ambiguity and changing priorities in response to business needs
  • You prefer working in highly structured, process-heavy environments
  • You're not interested in contributing to recruitment and team-building efforts

  • 5+ years of software development experience: you have a strong technical background with broad knowledge of software development

  • Strong communication skills, both technical and non-technical
  • Ability to balance technical considerations with business objectives
  • Experience with software development lifecycles and best practices
  • Problem-solving skills and ability to manage complex projects

Our Team

Instead of being siloed, Eng and QA work hand-in-hand with Product and Design for execution of new ideas and solutions. Our Eng team includes people from all levels of seniority and with a variety of backgrounds, from Fortune 500 to startups to FinTech to bootcamps.

jobs.excerpt: Remote Raven is hiring a GL Accountant for a long-established US community association management company headquartered in the Mountain time zone.
jobs.description:
Remote Raven is hiring a GL Accountant for a long-established US community association management company headquartered in the Mountain time zone. Their communities are large, master-planned and long-lived, and the people who manage them on the ground depend on a small offsite accounting team to tell them where each community actually stands.

You would own that answer for a portfolio of associations. Monthly, quarterly and annual statements. The accruals that make a month honest. Bank and balance sheet reconciliations that tie. Budgets, and the variance conversations that follow them. Setting up communities as they come on, and closing them out cleanly when they go. You would also review and approve work prepared by other accountants, which means your judgment is the last check before numbers reach a board.

This role takes a different level of trust than a production accounting seat. Boards are volunteers who read your statements and make real decisions from them. Community managers call you when an owner is upset about a number. You will be asked to explain, sometimes to defend, and occasionally to say plainly that something was wrong and here is the correction. It suits someone who is precise, unflappable and quick to respond.

Financial Reporting & Month-End Close

  • Prepare monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements for a portfolio of community associations.
  • Record monthly expense accruals so each period carries the costs that actually belong to it.
  • Assemble complete financial packages for board presentations and management review.
  • Maintain audit-ready workpapers that support every number in the statements.
  • Hit a fixed monthly close calendar across several communities at the same time.

Review & Quality Control

  • Review and approve financial work prepared by other members of the accounting team.
  • Catch errors before they reach a board packet, rather than after a board member finds them.
  • Keep treatment consistent across every community in the portfolio.

Reconciliations & Balance Sheet Integrity

  • Perform monthly bank reconciliations for operating and reserve accounts.
  • Reconcile other balance sheet accounts and resolve differences properly instead of forcing them to balance.
  • Keep reserve funds and operating funds correctly separated at all times.

Budgets & Variance Analysis

  • Review, prepare, enter, track and report community budgets.
  • Flag variances against budget and identify what is actually driving them.
  • Support the annual budget preparation cycle.

Community Setup, Transitions & Terminations

  • Set up new communities and their accounts as they come on board.
  • Process community terminations, including the final reconciliation and clean handover.
  • Maintain accurate, complete and retrievable financial records throughout.

Client & Stakeholder Communication

  • Handle a high volume of calls and emails from the internal team, community managers and board members.
  • Explain financial statements to people who are not accountants, in language they can act on.
  • Stay calm and professional in difficult conversations and with strong personalities.
  • Respond quickly. Responsiveness is a core expectation of this seat, not a bonus.

Requirements

  • An active CPA license.
  • Strong working knowledge of GAAP, applied in a community association or comparable multi-entity environment.
  • A demonstrated ability to carry high volume across multiple client accounts without accuracy slipping.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel for reconciliations, budget tracking and financial reporting, plus solid Microsoft Word.
  • Strong written and verbal English, including the ability to explain numbers to non-financial readers.
  • Availability to work full time on a US Mountain Standard Time schedule.
  • A reliable home setup: a working computer, stable high-speed internet and a backup connection.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with homeowner association (HOA) or community association accounting.
  • Experience on a community association management platform such as Vantaca, TOPS, CINC, Jenark or Caliber.
  • Experience presenting or explaining financials to a board, committee or non-financial manager.
  • Experience with reserve fund accounting and the operating/reserve fund split.
  • Experience closing many entities on a fixed monthly calendar.

Tools & Software

  • Microsoft Excel (advanced) and Microsoft Word
  • A community association or property accounting platform (Vantaca, TOPS, CINC, Jenark, Caliber or comparable)
  • General ledger / ERP accounting software
  • Online banking portals for reconciliation
  • Microsoft Teams and OneDrive
  • Hubstaff time tracking, which is standard on every Remote Raven placement

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You reconcile to zero. When something does not tie, you find out why rather than forcing it.
  • You would rather flag a problem early and be wrong than stay quiet and be right.
  • You can explain a variance to someone who has never read a financial statement, without making them feel stupid.
  • You stay level when a board member is upset, and you do not take it personally.
  • You own a mistake out loud, quickly, and usually with the correction already in hand.
  • You are comfortable being the person who catches what everyone else missed.
  • You answer. Quickly. Even when the answer is "I am on it, you will have it Thursday."

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Up to $10/hour
  • 100% remote work
  • Full-time role We hire for the long haul, so a steady track record of staying and growing always moves you up our list.

To apply

Ensure your LinkedIn profile and resume are up-to-date and comprehensive (submit a comprehensive resume in English, PDF format).

A quick note on how we will reach you: our recruitment team communicates primarily through Telegram, using the mobile number on your application and resume. Please make sure that number is active and registered on Telegram, since this is where screening and interview scheduling happen. If it is not registered yet, you can set it up right after you apply — it takes only a few minutes and keeps your application moving without delay.

By applying, you consent to being contacted via the contact information provided in your application for recruitment purposes only.

Because of the volume of applications we receive, we’re only able to follow up directly with candidates whose experience closely matches this role. If you don’t hear from us within 10 days, please know we genuinely appreciate your interest—and we’d welcome your application to future openings that may be a stronger fit. Thank you for considering Remote Raven, and all the best in your search.

A note on scheduling: initial interviews run in US Mountain Standard Time (MST) within a 3:00 AM – 1:00 PM MST window. We know that takes flexibility around the time difference, and we genuinely appreciate it.

jobs.excerpt: Flex is building the AI-native private bank for super premium, closely held business owners.
jobs.description:
Flex is building the AI-native private bank for super premium, closely held business owners.

We are re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs. From the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, financial operations, all rebuilt from the ground up as a single intelligent system.

Since launching publicly in September 2023, we have scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.

Our customers are affluent business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue. The backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. We are replacing the outdated banks and fragmented tools they are stuck with. The opportunity is a roughly $1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. We are building toward $100B+ in enterprise value by delivering a product that is fundamentally better, not incrementally improved.

Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.

What we hold ourselves to: mission-critical problems, high bar low ego, speed over comfort, enduring impact.

Locations: Remote. Open to candidates in Canada, Mexico, the United States, Brazil, and Colombia.

The Role

You will own Flex's Accountants Stack. Accounting integrations, expense management, bill pay, invoicing, AR and AP, and financial reporting. The full set of tools that closely held business owners and the accountants who serve them use to run the financial operations of the company.

The accountant is the lead persona for this role. Bookkeepers, controllers, fractional CFOs, and outside CPAs are the people who actually live in this software day to day. Build for them and the owner wins by default. Build only for the owner and the accountant works around you, which means you lose.

The reason this role exists at Flex and not at every fintech is the unique customer we serve. Super premium business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue have a controller or an outside accountant, real ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, sometimes Microsoft Dynamics or Acumatica), and a layered financial life where the business and personal sides are deeply intertwined. The owner pays themselves a distribution, then funds personal investments, then pays for an asset, then expenses something back through the company. Their accountant has to make all of it tie out. We are the only product positioned to make that integrated life elegant for both sides. This role builds it.

You will not build a generic accounting integration. You will build the Accountants Stack that bookkeepers, controllers, and CPAs actually want, which means knowing what they hate about QuickBooks, what they love about NetSuite, what they wish Bill.com did, and where the seams between business and personal finance create the most friction today.

What you will do

Define the strategy and own the connectivity layer to the accounting and ERP systems our customers' accountants use. QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, etc.

Build expense management that works for owners and the accountants reconciling on their behalf. Receipt capture, GL coding, approval workflows, integration into the accounting tools without requiring manual reconciliation downstream.

Own bill pay and AR/AP. The workflow from invoice received to vendor paid, from invoice sent to customer paid, with full reconciliation back to the accounting system.

Build the invoicing product. We do not have a real invoicing offering today and customers are starting to ask. Decide what shape it takes and ship it.

Architect the connection between business financial data and personal financial data. This is the wedge no other fintech has. Make the integrated owner life real in product so the accountant can deliver it cleanly.

Partner closely with the Banking, Credit, Cards, and Payments product owners so financial flows tie out cleanly across the stack. No seams. No reconciliation tax for the accountant or the customer.

Translate the controller, CFO, and CPA persona for the rest of the company. We need someone who speaks both owner and accountant fluently. And can translate it to the owner mindset.

What you will need

You have spent years thinking about how business owners and the accountants who serve them actually run financial operations. You know the difference between a bookkeeper, a controller, a fractional CFO, and an outside accountant, and you have built product for at least one of them.

Deep, hands-on familiarity with at least two of: QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica. Not "I know they exist." Actually built in or integrated to them at depth.

You can journal a transaction without looking it up. You understand accrual versus cash basis, the close cycle, what a 1099 is for, and why a controller cares about the audit trail.

You have built either inside an accounting platform, on top of one as an integration partner, or built a fintech product that lives natively in the accounting workflow.

You understand the accountant channel and how CPAs influence product adoption. Bonus if you have built for or partnered with CPAs directly.

Typically 4 to 10 years of experience. Title is not the point.

We want to hear from you. We value passion, determination, and honesty. If you do not match every line of the spec but you can show us the work, apply anyway. Unusual paths and rare skills are how you stand out at Flex.

Head of Sales (Player-Coach) – Fleet Safety Training

If you are a hands-on sales builder who still wants to carry a number, coach rising sellers, and shape the go-to-market engine—not just inherit someone else’s playbook—this is a high-visibility opportunity to lead growth for a long-established, PE-backed safety training and software company. You’ll sell directly into public-sector and commercial fleet environments while building the process, cadence, and team capability needed to scale recurring revenue nationwide.

The Opportunity

This company has served safety-focused organizations for decades and supports more than 3,000 active customers across commercial fleets, state and local government, EMS, fire departments, logistics, warehouses, school bus operators, and other vehicle-intensive environments. Following a recent private-equity acquisition, the business has upgraded its technology and launched a recurring training platform designed for larger fleets.

Now the company is ready to expand new-customer growth, increase share of wallet, and build a more repeatable sales motion. This role is part seller, part coach, and part architect: you’ll own meaningful revenue directly while helping junior sellers improve how they prospect, qualify, navigate stakeholders, and close.

Role Snapshot

  • Location: Remote within the United States
  • Territory: Nationwide U.S.
  • Employment Type: Full-time
  • Compensation: $110,000–$120,000 base salary with a 50/50 split; target OTE around $220,000, with stretch potential around $240,000
  • Travel: As needed for industry events, trade shows, and key customer meetings
  • Team Scope: Lead and coach a small sales team, including junior sellers and SDR support
  • Individual Quota: Expected around $300,000–$400,000

What You Will Own

Carry and Close Your Own Book

  • Build a nationwide pipeline across public-sector and commercial accounts.
  • Prospect, qualify, run discovery, navigate stakeholders, and close new business.
  • Sell safety training, compliance, and software-enabled training solutions into EMS, fire, fleet, logistics, warehouse, transportation, and related environments.
  • Manage deal sizes that commonly range from $5,000–$20,000, with larger opportunities reaching roughly $75,000 and some government deals requiring longer procurement cycles.
  • Engage buyers ranging from day-to-day safety and training operators to fleet executives, finance leaders, and other senior stakeholders.
  • Develop partnerships with insurance, risk, safety, membership, and industry organizations.
  • Represent the company at trade shows and industry events.

Coach and Build the Sales Team

  • Coach junior AEs and SDR-level talent through call reviews, deal strategy, shadowing, and timely feedback.
  • Help sellers improve qualification, objection handling, stakeholder mapping, follow-up, and close strategy.
  • Support recovery plans for stalled deals and complex multi-stakeholder opportunities.
  • Create a practical sales playbook, operating cadence, scripts, messaging, and repeatable process.
  • Keep HubSpot clean, accurate, and useful for forecasting and team visibility.
  • Report pipeline, forecast, and revenue progress to executive leadership.
  • Help hire and onboard future sellers as the function grows.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You have 5+ years of Account Executive or sales leadership experience in public-sector, government-adjacent, commercial SaaS, training, compliance, fleet, transportation, safety, risk, or another transferable B2B environment.
  • You have owned complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles and can show evidence of creating pipeline, advancing deals, and closing business.
  • You have directly managed or meaningfully coached BDRs, SDRs, junior AEs, or early-career sales talent.
  • You are still energized by selling yourself—not just inspecting someone else’s forecast.

Department Overview

The Tax & Compliance Department is a component of the OHSU Finance Division, responsible for complex compliance, regulatory tax withholding, tax reporting and other reporting/filing to federal and states entities and other applicable outside entities. The Tax & Compliance Department functions include research and implementation of federal and multi-state regulations related to tax, wage and hour, unemployment and other tax aspects related to payroll including out-of-state payroll. The Tax & Compliance department also maintains, writes and updates OHSU financial policies and procedures; ensures states and federal regulatory compliance standards are met, ensures proper record retention for tax related documents; establishes guidelines for disaster recovery.

The department's responsibilities also include coordinating external reporting for the institution, functioning as a resource for tax items and tax reporting items, resolving tax issues. The department is also responsible for training and providing support to the departments across the organization. Responsibilities of the department also include testing and implementation of tax related system upgrades and system implementation.

Function/Duties of Position

Institutional Tax Compliance & Reporting

Responsible for the timely and accurate preparation, filing, payment, and administration of federal, state, and local tax obligations for OHSU and its subsidiaries. Performs complex research, analysis, compliance monitoring, and risk assessment activities to support regulatory compliance and provide guidance on the tax implications of organizational activities involving high complexity and risk.

  • Prepare, reconcile, and file the unrelated business income tax return, including gathering financial and operational information to support filings, ensuring compliance with federal and various state laws and regulations.
  • Review institutional activities for potential unrelated business income and serve as the liaison with external tax consultants for preparation of the 990-T.
  • Assist departments in identifying and addressing tax compliance issues associated with new programs, contracts, grants, sponsorships, revenue generating activities, and other institutional initiatives and advise Director on risks and mitigation.
  • Prepare, reconcile, and file indirect tax returns, including gathering financial and operational information to support filings, ensuring compliance with federal and various state laws and regulations specific to excise, sales, use, franchise, occupational, real property, tangible property, and others as necessary.
  • Prepare, reconcile, and file business tax returns for OHSU subsidiaries, maintain accurate records, ensuring compliance with partnership and corporate tax laws.
  • Maintain and update annual IRS Form W-9s for OHSU and subsidiaries.
  • Prepare, reconcile, and file Form 945 for domestic income tax withholding.
  • Perform proactive periodic compliance pre-audits, risk assessments and ongoing compliance monitoring to actively review systems, processes, and documentation to identify and address potential issues and risks.
  • Process and oversee tax payment and deposit activities, ensuring accurate and timely compliance with regulatory requirements and managing refunds.
  • Respond to related tax correspondence including audits and notices, research issues as they arise, collect documentation and data required by external taxing authorities, review and analyze documents and data to ensure completeness, accuracy and compliance with regulations and OHSU’s internal controls.

International Tax Compliance & Reporting

Independently administer international tax compliance activities, coordinating with team members, and conducting complex research analysis to ensure adherence to applicable tax and immigration-related requirements.

  • Maintain nonresident alien tax compliance records and documentation for international employees, students, scholars, and visitors.
  • Administer tax treaty analysis, implementation, and compliance and maintain applicable tax software records and documentation.
  • Collect, review, and maintain visa, immigration, residency, scholarship, fellowship, and grant documentation to ensure compliance.
  • Ensure compliance with federal tax withholding, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements applicable to international employees, students, scholars, and visitors.
  • Prepare Forms 1042 and 1042-S and review payments to foreign nationals and foreign vendors for proper withholding and reporting.
  • Prepare, file, and maintain OHSU tax residency certificate.
  • Assist departments with questions related to international tax compliance.
  • Respond to related correspondence and research issues as they arise.

Regulatory Compliance & Reporting

Independently prepares, reconciles, files, and administers regulatory reports and related reporting requirements, ensuring compliance with federal, state, and other applicable regulations.

  • Prepare, reconcile, and file regulatory reports including quarterly and annual filings with federal and state regulatory agencies, maintaining accurate files and clear audit trail, ensuring compliance with reporting and timely filing of reports with authorities.
  • Gather reporting and information to support filings, ensuring compliance with federal and various state laws and regulations specific for the U.S. Census Bureau, U.S. Department of Labor, State of Oregon and other authorities as needed.
  • Conducts compliance audits, risk assessments and periodic compliance monitoring.
  • Process accurate and timely payments as needed and manage refunds.
  • Respond to related correspondence and research issues as they arise.

Compliance Monitoring, Audit & Bargaining Support, & Policy Development

Evaluate, maintain, and develop fiscal policies, guidelines, frequently asked questions, and procedures, collaborating with stakeholders across the organization, to ensure compliance with federal and state laws and regulations as well as OHSU policies and guidelines.

  • Evaluate fiscal policies, guidelines, procedures and business practices for efficiency, effectiveness, compliance, and continuous improvement, identifying and recommending changes to the Director as needed.
  • Support collective bargaining activities by providing research, analysis, and technical expertise during negotiations, assisting with implementation and administration of bargaining agreement provisions, and ensuring organizational compliance with applicable collective bargaining agreements, policies, and regulatory requirements.
  • Conduct audit readiness assessments, compliance reviews, and gap analyses to evaluate adherence to regulatory requirements, policies, procedures, and internal controls; identify areas of risk; and recommend corrective actions and process improvements.
  • Contribute to growing the organization’s knowledge and compliance in areas of tax and audit.
  • Propose updates to applicable policies, guidelines and procedures as needed to prevent and address areas of non-compliance and reduce risk.
  • Provide superior customer service to internal and external contacts.

Continued Professional Development

Participate in appropriate activities that enhance general knowledge of or ability to do assigned work including but not limited to: attend classes, e-learning classes, seminars, and other training forums; job shadow; attend staff meetings and other informational sessions; read vendor documentation, federal and states resources related to tax, or other sources appropriate to position; interact with peers and other employees to receive and disseminate information.

In a self-directed fashion, is responsible for keeping current with changes to federal and state tax law and related legislation, as well as changes to OHSU Code of Conduct, polices, union agreements, letters of agreement, and memorandum of understanding documents.

Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or tax-related field, or equivalent education/experience.

  • Minimum 5 years of experience with tax compliance and reporting in federal and multi-state business taxes, specifically unrelated business income tax for healthcare, government, higher education, or nonprofit tax areas.

Skills and Abilities

  • Knowledge of federal, state, local, and international income tax compliance requirements.

jobs.description:
Risk Model Engineer — Gas Distribution Integrity

Location: Remote (US or Canada)
Department: Insights (AI/ML)
Reports to: Data Science Team Lead

About the Role

Irth is building a new AI-driven threat and risk management platform for pipeline asset integrity. The platform brings together three capabilities that have never previously lived in one place at Irth:

  • A governed, cross-product data platform built on Databricks and Azure.
  • An AI-powered ingestion layer that normalizes, repairs, and enriches customer data without services-heavy onboarding.
  • A reusable analytical layer that runs industry-standard, Irth-developed, and customer-built risk models against that data.

We are hiring a Risk Model Engineer to own the gas distribution risk models within that analytical layer.

Distribution is a new model domain for the platform. The threat framework and model set are being defined now in collaboration with subject-matter experts and design-partner operators. In this role, you will help define the models, build them, and take them through validation—producing outputs that utilities can use to prioritize replacement programs and support regulatory proceedings.

The modeling work focuses on large populations of buried assets with relatively few observed failures, incomplete records, and limited direct inspection data. The work spans physics-based probabilistic models and machine learning, with an emphasis on producing risk rankings that remain explainable, calibrated, and defensible.

You will own the model content: what the model computes, why it computes it, and the evidence supporting its validity.

Productionization—including model serving, data pipelines, deployment, and monitoring infrastructure—is owned by dedicated ML Ops and data engineering roles with whom you will work closely.

Key Responsibilities

1. Threat Framework & Integration

  • Translate the gas distribution threat framework, in collaboration with subject-matter experts, into systematic threat identification methods and supporting data structures.
  • Integrate model inputs from diverse datasets across Irth's product offerings.
  • Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and limitations in source data and determine how they should be reflected in model inputs and outputs.

2. Model Development

  • Extend threat coverage across domains, including:
    • Legacy material corrosion
    • Plastic embrittlement
    • Excavation damage
    • Cross-bores
    • Other gas distribution

Requirements

Skills We're Hiring For

We are hiring across a broad range of capabilities and do not expect a single candidate to have all of them. We are looking for strong depth in one or more areas and the curiosity and judgment to work across the others.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Gas distribution integrity management — program design, threat identification under 49 CFR Part 192, Subpart P, and replacement prioritization, from the operator, consultancy, regulator, or technology-vendor side.
  • Legacy material risk — cast iron, bare steel, vintage plastics, and plastic embrittlement.
  • Leak survey, methane detection, and cross-bore programs.
  • Machine learning applied to physical asset data, including time-series, survival, anomaly-detection, and classification models trainer

Benefits

  • Competitive Salary – A competitive compensation package based on experience and qualifications.
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance – Comprehensive insurance coverage to support you and your family.
  • 401(k) Plan with Company Match.
  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) – Time off to support work-life balance and personal needs.
  • Company-Paid Holidays – Paid holidays throughout the year.
  • Flexible Work Options – Work-from-home opportunities are available, depending on role and business needs.
  • On-Call Compensation – Additional pay for eligible on-call shifts.

Kickstarter is the leading crowdfunding platform for creative projects across film, games, music, art, design, and technology. Since our founding in 2009, our mission to help bring creative projects to life has been powered by the people behind the work.

Kickstarter is seeking an experienced Director, Tax to lead our tax function and set the strategic direction for tax across the company and its subsidiaries globally. This role is focused on indirect tax (e.g., VAT, GST, and sales tax) strategy related to Kickstarter’s marketplace sales products. Direct tax matters will also sit under this role. You'll be the company's primary internal tax authority, advising executive leadership and collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders including legal, product, and finance on the tax implications of new markets, product offerings, and structures, while modernizing and scaling Kickstarter's tax technology and processes for our global user base. This is a high-visibility role for a strategic tax leader who is highly curious, stays ahead of evolving tax guidance across jurisdictions, and wants to build a function, not just run one.

Candidates based in the United States and United Kingdom are strongly preferred.

The salary range for this role in the United States is $185,000 - 225,000.

  • Own the company's global indirect tax strategy globally, setting priorities and risk tolerance in partnership with Finance and Legal leadership.
  • Build, manage, and develop a tax team, establishing standards, workflows, and career development paths as the function scales.
  • Set the roadmap for the Company's tax technology stack (including Avalara and adjacent tools), leading automation and process initiatives that reduce manual operations and support global expansion.
  • Design and implement indirect tax processes and controls purpose-built for a marketplace model, drawing on prior experience standing up this kind of process at another marketplace or online platform.
  • Serve as the primary relationship owner for the Company's external tax advisors across jurisdictions, directing engagement priorities and ensuring advice and assumed risk are clearly communicated to executive stakeholders.
  • Act as the primary resource when assessing tax impact and explaining Kickstarter’s tax policy with strategic new and existing creators and high value partners
  • Ultimately own the accuracy, timeliness, and integrity of VAT, sales tax, and corporate filings across all applicable jurisdictions, overseeing the team and advisors who execute them.
  • Partner directly with Legal, Product, and executive leadership to evaluate and structure the tax implications of new offerings, markets, and business models, including entity structuring and cross-border considerations.
  • Own transfer pricing policy and documentation across subsidiaries, in partnership with external advisors.
  • Lead the Company's response to tax notices and audits, including managing outside counsel and advisors on higher-stakes or multi-jurisdiction matters.
  • Partner with the Insights team to establish reconciliation standards between internal data and filed returns, and resolve discrepancies at a structural level.
  • Direct product testing standards for tax calculation accuracy as the Company launches new features or expands into new jurisdictions.
  • Own the tax input into the Company's audited financial statements, partnering with Accounting leadership on technical positions, disclosures, and month-end close for all tax-related entries.

About You

WORK TYPE: Remote

HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

The Senior Manager, Product Developmentis responsible for leading the execution of product development strategies for custom sports uniforms and apparel from client intake through commercialization and production readiness. This role oversees a team of development professionals while ensuring alignment with adidas brand standards, client requirements, development timelines, cost objectives, quality expectations, and manufacturing capabilities.

The Senior Manager serves as the primary Product Development liaison for assigned adidas business areas, partnering closely with adidas stakeholders and internal Technical Design, Pattern, Artwork, Costing, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. This role drives cross-functional alignment, process improvement, team development, and executional excellence while supporting the continued growth and scalability of the Custom Outfitters development organization.

The Senior Manager manages a portfolio of custom uniform development programs and is accountable for ensuring projects are delivered on time, within established cost and margin expectations, and in accordance with adidas quality and performance standards. This position provides operational leadership, resolves development escalations, and makes recommendations regarding resources, processes, capacity, and organizational needs.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Product Development Leadership

  • Lead the execution of custom sports uniform and apparel development across assigned adidas accounts, programs, and product categories.

  • Lead product development planning and execution from client intake and concept translation through sampling, approvals, production readiness, and commercialization, ensuring adherence to key milestones, deliverables, development calendars, and launch timelines.

Cross Functional Collaboration

  • Serve as the primary Product Development liaison to assigned adidas stakeholders, ensuring alignment with brand standards, product expectations, development requirements, timelines, and issue resolution.

  • Partner with internal teams and manufacturing partners to transition approved concepts and prototypes into scalable, cost-efficient production.

  • Partner with Costing, Finance, commercial leadership, and operational teams to monitor development costs, margin performance, resource requirements, and financial risks.

Operational Excellence

  • Establish, maintain, and optimize product development processes, tools, documentation, and best practices to improve efficiency, quality, speed to market, and scalability.

  • Monitor development performance through KPIs and reporting related to delivery, quality, productivity, cost, capacity, and client service.

Business & Strategic Contribution

  • Support long-term development planning, resource strategies, workforce planning, and organizational initiatives for assigned adidas programs.

Leadership & Team Development

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

Job Title: Senior Full Stack Software Engineer (Product & Infrastructure)

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
