jobs.title: Digital Literacy Educator / Formateur-trice en litteracie numerique
jobs.excerpt: Who we areSince 2013, Digital Moment has led digital education for Canadian youth, expanding the reach and impact of our foundational programs each year.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Since 2013, Digital Moment has led digital education for Canadian youth, expanding the reach and impact of our foundational programs each year.

But we don’t stop there—we innovate to equip youth with the skills to harness emerging technologies and tackle pressing societal challenges.

We are shaping AI-fluent leaders for a future-ready Canada with our innovative programs and initiatives.

We are driven by innovation, inclusion, and impact, empowering the next generation to shape technology for good. Working with us means making a difference every day by equipping youth with essential digital skills to navigate a technology-driven world.

We are a fully-remote, small and mighty, team that embraces innovation, challenges the status quo and experiments with new ideas to drive meaningful change. We’ve built a culture that is positive, collaborative and focused on the purpose we want to create.

We’re currently looking for Digital Literacy Educators to join our team.

Here’s an Overview of the Position

Digital Moment is seeking experienced educators, facilitators, and relationship-builders to support the growth and adoption of AI literacy initiatives across Canada. As part of a national cohort, each Digital Literacy Educator will lead a region and will drive engagement within specific territories.

This role focuses on educator professional development, stakeholder outreach, regional relationship-building, and practical knowledge mobilization. Working directly with educators, school boards, ministries of education, educational associations, and local partners, you will build awareness, pitch Digital Moment’s AI Literacy Framework, deliver high-impact professional learning, and move aligned opportunities from conversation into action.

While you will need a strong understanding of Digital Moment’s AI Literacy Framework (training we, and our international partner, will provide) to present and contextualize it for key stakeholders, your primary day-to-day focus will be driving regional outreach, facilitating workshops, building local educator networks, and supporting practical implementation in K-12 (elementary school) contexts.

Key Responsibilities

Regional Outreach & Partnership Mobilization

  • Develop and maintain relationships with educators, school leaders, school boards, ministries, educational associations, and other key stakeholders across your region.
  • Initiate outreach meetings to understand emerging needs, regional priorities, and local challenges, serving as a trusted ambassador for Digital Moment’s AI literacy initiatives.
  • Pitch Digital Moment’s AI Literacy Framework and educational programs to system leaders, demonstrating how AI literacy can be ethically integrated into teaching, leadership, and policy.
  • Identify and cultivate local champions, collaborators, and partnership opportunities to extend reach across the regional education ecosystem.
  • Help move aligned opportunities into active projects through clear next steps, shared workplans, and formal partnership structures.
  • Identify existing regional resources and initiatives that can be leveraged or supported rather than duplicated.

Educator Professional Development & Community Building

  • Deliver engaging, practical workshops, webinars, and learning sessions (both virtual and in-person) that help educators apply AI literacy concepts in classroom contexts.
  • Adapt professional learning content for diverse audiences, including classroom teachers, school administrators, and system-level decision-makers.
  • Build and nurture regional educator networks to foster peer learning, shared practice, ongoing feedback, and sustained engagement post-training.
  • Develop follow-up pathways (check-ins, resource sharing, community conversations) that help educators progress from initial awareness to applied classroom practice.

Thought Leadership & Sector Representation

  • Represent Digital Moment at regional conferences, webinars, consultations, and sector conversations related to AI literacy and digital education.
  • Promote Digital Moment’s initiatives as a connected body of work, illustrating how our framework, training, resources, and outreach reinforce one another.
  • Contribute informed perspectives on emerging AI and education trends, helping position Digital Moment as a practical, ethical, and educator-informed voice.
  • Help identify opportunities to strengthen Digital Moment’s visibility, credibility, and reach within your regional education ecosystem.

Monitoring, Tracking & Field Feedback

  • Maintain practical systems for documenting outreach, relationship pipelines, training delivery, and follow-up actions.
  • Gather ground-level feedback from training participants, administrators, and regional partners to share actionable insights with our internal product and framework teams.
  • Track indicators of reach, engagement, learning needs, and partnership progress against agreed regional targets.
  • Prepare regular updates and summaries for leadership that highlight progress, upcoming actions, regional barriers, decisions needed, and lessons learned.

Ideal Candidate Profile

  • Experience
    • Experience as a K-12 (elementary school) educator, instructional leader, consultant, or education sector professional.
    • Demonstrated experience engaging with educators, school leaders, boards, ministries, or education organizations within your target region.
    • Deep cultural knowledge, networks, and demonstrated experience working directly within the Francophone education community and school system in Quebec.
    • Experience facilitating meetings, workshops, webinars, advisory groups, or stakeholder consultations (both virtual and in-person).
    • Experience building professional relationships, partnerships, and collaborative workplans.
    • Experience supporting partnership processes, including memoranda of understanding, shared implementation plans, or formal agreements.
  • Knowledge
    • Strong understanding of K-12 education systems, curriculum frameworks, and educational change processes within your designated territory.
    • Basic knowledge of AI literacy, digital literacy, emerging technologies, or related fields, and how to make these concepts accessible to educators. We will continue to learn together.
    • Familiarity with current opportunities, priorities, and operational challenges facing educators and school systems today.
  • Skills
    • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills in English and in French.
    • Strong workshop facilitation, public speaking, and relationship-building abilities.
    • Strong critical thinking and strategic problem-solving skills to navigate regional nuances.
    • Ability to identify partnership opportunities, connect stakeholders, and translate ideas into clear actions.
  • Personal Attributes
    • Curious, proactive, and self-directed, with the ability to work independently while collaborating across a national team.
    • Comfortable navigating ambiguity, emerging opportunities, and shifting technology landscapes.
    • Diplomatic and respectful while willing to ask challenging questions and explore new approaches.
    • Mission-driven with a commitment to helping educators and learners thrive in an AI-enabled world.
    • Collaborative mindset with a strong belief in partnership, shared impact, and community engagement.
    • Willingness to undertake periodic regional travel for in-person workshops, partner meetings, and sector events.

If this sounds like you - we want to hear from you!

Here’s what we offer our employees:

  • Fully remote work
  • Competitive salary
  • Generous time off policy (10 wellness days and 20 days of vacation annually)
  • Health benefits: benefits coverage as of Day 1
  • Matching RRSP contribution program

Qui sommes-nous?

Depuis 2013, Digital Moment est un chef de file en éducation numérique auprès des jeunes canadiens. Chaque année, nous élargissons la portée et l’impact de nos programmes.

Mais nous ne nous arrêtons pas là. Nous innovons afin de donner aux jeunes les compétences nécessaires pour tirer parti des technologies émergentes et relever certains des défis sociaux les plus urgents de notre époque.

Grâce à nos programmes et initiatives novateurs, nous contribuons à former des leaders qui maîtrisent l’intelligence artificielle et qui sont prêts à bâtir le Canada de demain.

Notre travail repose sur trois valeurs fondamentales : l’innovation, l’inclusion et l’impact. Nous donnons à la prochaine génération les moyens de façonner la technologie pour le bien collectif. Travailler chez Digital Moment, c’est avoir l’occasion de faire une différence chaque jour en donnant aux jeunes les compétences numériques essentielles pour évoluer dans un monde où la technologie occupe une place centrale.

Nous sommes une petite équipe dynamique et ambitieuse qui travaille entièrement à distance. Nous valorisons l’innovation, remettons en question les façons de faire établies et expérimentons de nouvelles idées afin de créer des changements significatifs. Nous avons bâti une culture positive et collaborative, axée sur la mission et l’impact que nous souhaitons créer.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche de formateur·trice·s en littératie numérique pour se joindre à notre équipe.

Aperçu du poste

Digital Moment est à la recherche de personnes expérimentées en enseignement, en animation et en développement de relations pour soutenir la croissance et l’adoption d’initiatives en littératie de l’intelligence artificielle partout au Canada. Au sein d’une équipe nationale, chaque formateur·trice en littératie numérique sera responsable d’une région et mobilisera les acteurs et actrices clés de son territoire.

Le rôle est axé sur le développement professionnel du personnel éducatif, la mobilisation des parties prenantes, le développement de relations à l’échelle régionale et le partage de connaissances pratiques.

En travaillant directement avec le personnel enseignant, les centres de services scolaires, les ministères de l’Éducation, les associations du milieu de l’éducation et les partenaires locaux, vous contribuerez à faire connaître les initiatives de Digital Moment, à présenter notre cadre de référence en littératie de l’IA, à offrir des activités de développement professionnel à fort impact et à faire passer les occasions de collaboration de la discussion à l’action.

Vous devrez bien comprendre le cadre de référence de Digital Moment en littératie de l’IA — une formation vous sera offerte par Digital Moment et notre partenaire international — afin de pouvoir le présenter et le contextualiser auprès des principales parties prenantes.

Toutefois, votre travail quotidien portera principalement sur la mobilisation régionale, l’animation d’ateliers, la création de réseaux locaux de personnel éducatif et le soutien à la mise en œuvre concrète de la littératie de l’IA dans les milieux scolaires de la maternelle au secondaire.

Principales responsabilités

Mobilisation régionale et développement de partenariats

  • Développer et maintenir des relations avec le personnel enseignant, les directions d’établissement, les centres de services scolaires, les ministères, les associations du milieu de l’éducation et les autres parties prenantes clés de votre région.
  • Organiser des rencontres de mobilisation afin de comprendre les besoins émergents, les priorités régionales et les enjeux locaux, tout en agissant comme ambassadeur·drice de confiance des initiatives de Digital Moment en littératie de l’IA.
  • Présenter le cadre de référence de Digital Moment en littératie de l’IA et ses programmes éducatifs aux décideurs et décideuses du milieu de l’éducation, en démontrant comment la littératie de l’IA peut être intégrée de façon éthique à l’enseignement, au leadership scolaire et aux politiques éducatives.
  • Identifier et mobiliser des personnes ambassadrices, des collaborateurs·trices et des occasions de partenariat afin d’accroître la portée de Digital Moment dans l’écosystème éducatif régional.
  • Faire progresser les occasions de collaboration vers des projets concrets grâce à des échéanciers clairs, des plans de travail communs et des structures de partenariat formelles.
  • Recenser les ressources et initiatives déjà présentes dans la région qui pourraient être mises à profit ou soutenues, plutôt que reproduites.

Développement professionnel du personnel éducatif et création de communautés

  • Animer des ateliers, webinaires et activités d’apprentissage stimulants et pratiques, en mode virtuel ou en personne, qui aident le personnel éducatif à appliquer les concepts de littératie de l’IA dans des contextes pédagogiques concrets.
  • Adapter le contenu de développement professionnel à différents publics, notamment le personnel enseignant, les directions d’établissement et les personnes responsables de décisions à l’échelle du système scolaire.
  • Développer et faire vivre des réseaux régionaux de personnel éducatif afin de favoriser l’apprentissage entre pairs, le partage de pratiques, la rétroaction continue et l’engagement à long terme après les formations.
  • Mettre en place des mécanismes de suivi — rencontres de suivi, partage de ressources, échanges au sein de la communauté — afin d’aider le personnel éducatif à passer de la sensibilisation initiale à l’application concrète en classe.

Leadership d’opinion et représentation dans le secteur

  • Représenter Digital Moment lors de conférences régionales, de webinaires, de consultations et de discussions sectorielles portant sur la littératie de l’IA et l’éducation numérique.
  • Présenter les initiatives de Digital Moment comme un ensemble cohérent, en démontrant comment notre cadre de référence, nos formations, nos ressources et nos activités de mobilisation se renforcent mutuellement.
  • Contribuer à la réflexion sur les tendances émergentes en matière d’IA et d’éducation et aider à positionner Digital Moment comme une voix pratique, éthique et ancrée dans les réalités du personnel éducatif.
  • Repérer des occasions d’accroître la visibilité, la crédibilité et la portée de Digital Moment au sein de l’écosystème éducatif régional.

Suivi, documentation et rétroaction terrain

  • Maintenir des systèmes pratiques permettant de documenter les activités de mobilisation, le développement des relations et des partenariats, les formations offertes et les suivis à effectuer.
  • Recueillir les commentaires du personnel ayant participé aux formations, des gestionnaires et des partenaires régionaux afin de transmettre des informations concrètes et utiles aux équipes internes responsables des produits et du cadre de référence.
  • Suivre les indicateurs liés à la portée, à l’engagement, aux besoins d’apprentissage et à l’avancement des partenariats en fonction des objectifs régionaux établis.
  • Préparer régulièrement des mises à jour et des synthèses pour la direction, en faisant ressortir les progrès réalisés, les prochaines étapes, les obstacles régionaux, les décisions requises et les leçons apprises.

Profil recherché

Expérience

  • Expérience comme enseignant·e au primaire ou au secondaire, conseiller·ère pédagogique, leader pédagogique, consultant·e ou professionnel·le du secteur de l’éducation.
  • Expérience démontrée auprès du personnel enseignant, des directions d’établissement, des centres de services scolaires, des ministères ou d’organisations du milieu de l’éducation dans votre région.
  • Excellente connaissance de la culture, des réseaux et des réalités du milieu de l’éducation francophone au Québec, ainsi qu’une expérience concrète au sein du système scolaire québécois.
  • Expérience dans l’animation de rencontres, d’ateliers, de webinaires, de groupes consultatifs ou de consultations auprès de parties prenantes, en mode virtuel et en personne.
  • Expérience dans le développement de relations professionnelles, de partenariats et de plans de travail collaboratifs.
  • Expérience dans le soutien aux processus de partenariat, notamment la préparation de protocoles d’entente, de plans de mise en œuvre communs ou d’ententes officielles.

Connaissances

  • Bonne compréhension des systèmes d’éducation de la maternelle au secondaire, des cadres curriculaires et des processus de changement en éducation dans votre territoire.
  • Connaissances de base en littératie de l’IA, littératie numérique, technologies émergentes ou domaines connexes, ainsi que capacité à rendre ces concepts accessibles au personnel éducatif. Nous continuerons d’apprendre ensemble.
  • Bonne connaissance des occasions, des priorités et des défis opérationnels auxquels sont actuellement confrontés le personnel éducatif et les systèmes scolaires.

Compétences

  • Excellentes aptitudes en communication orale et écrite en français et en anglais.
  • Excellentes aptitudes en animation d’ateliers, en prise de parole en public et en développement de relations.
  • Fort esprit critique et excellente capacité à résoudre des problèmes de façon stratégique, en tenant compte des réalités propres à chaque région.
  • Capacité à repérer des occasions de partenariat, à mettre les parties prenantes en relation et à transformer les idées en actions concrètes.

Qualités personnelles

  • Personne curieuse, proactive et autonome, capable de travailler de façon indépendante tout en collaborant étroitement avec une équipe nationale.
  • À l’aise dans des contextes où les choses évoluent rapidement, avec des situations ambiguës, des occasions émergentes et un environnement technologique en constante évolution.
  • Diplomate et respectueux·euse, tout en étant à l’aise de poser des questions difficiles et d’explorer de nouvelles façons de faire.
  • Animé·e par la mission et profondément engagé·e à soutenir la réussite du personnel éducatif et des apprenant·e·s dans un monde propulsé par l’intelligence artificielle.
  • Esprit collaboratif et conviction profonde que les partenariats, l’impact collectif et l’engagement des communautés sont essentiels à la réussite.
  • Disponibilité pour effectuer des déplacements occasionnels dans la région afin d’animer des ateliers en personne, de rencontrer des partenaires et de participer à des événements sectoriels.

At STERRY, we’re not your average Growth Marketing Agency—we’re the rocket fuel behind crowdfunding and e-commerce success. Since day one, we’ve helped clients pull in over $100 million in trackable online revenue. We shatter limits, supercharge brands, and turn every click into cash.

STERRY is seeking a creative and data-driven Ad Graphic Designer to join our marketing team. In this role, you will be responsible for transforming strategic goals into high-impact visual narratives across multiple digital and print platforms.

The ideal candidate is a master of visual hierarchy, a meticulous photo editor, and a collaborative thinker who thrives in a fast-paced environment. You will play a pivotal role in maintaining brand consistency while pushing the boundaries of innovative ad design to drive performance.


What You'll Do:
  • Collaborate closely with the marketing and advertising teams to understand campaign objectives, target audience, and key messaging.

  • Creatives translation (DE/MX/UK/JA) - Translate promotional creatives while maintaining balance and harmony in the designs.

  • Global Perspective: Experience or comfort with localizing designs for international markets and working with multilingual typography.
  • Organization: Strong time-management skills and the ability to handle ad hoc tasks in a dynamic environment.

Why Join STERRY?
  • Fully remote position with flexible working hours.
  • Global Impact: See your designs come to life across major international markets.
  • Growth and development within a collaborative, innovative team.
  • A culture that values creativity, precision, and measurable results.

How to Apply:
Ready to create visuals drive global results? Send us your resume, cover letter, and a link to your portfolio showcasing your best advertising work.

Job Title: Email Marketing Specialist

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours (with flexibility for campaign launches and reporting deadlines)

About the Role

Our client is seeking an Email Marketing Specialist to build, launch, and optimize high-performing email campaigns that drive engagement, nurture leads, and generate measurable business results.

This role combines creative copywriting, audience segmentation, automation strategy, and technical ESP management. The Email Marketing Specialist owns the full email campaign lifecycle — from campaign planning and workflow automation to deliverability optimization and performance reporting.

The ideal candidate is analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable balancing creative messaging with performance-driven optimization.

Responsibilities

Campaign Development & Execution

  • Build and launch email campaigns using platforms such as HubSpot, Klaviyo, Marketo, Mailchimp, or ActiveCampaign
    • Write compelling subject lines, email copy, and calls-to-action tailored to audience segments
    • Design and optimize responsive email templates aligned with brand guidelines
    • Perform light HTML/CSS edits when necessary to improve formatting and rendering

Audience Segmentation & List Management

  • Maintain and organize email databases ranging from 20k–200k+ contacts
    • Segment audiences by lifecycle stage, engagement level, persona, geography, and behavioral data
    • Clean and maintain healthy email lists by removing inactive users, hard bounces, spam traps, and duplicates
    • Improve personalization strategies to increase engagement and conversion performance

Automation & Nurture Workflows

  • Build and maintain drip campaigns, nurture sequences, abandoned cart flows, onboarding workflows, and behavioral automations
    • Test workflow logic and trigger conditions to ensure campaigns function correctly
    • Continuously optimize automation flows to improve conversion rates and engagement

Deliverability & Compliance

  • Monitor sender reputation, inbox placement, and overall deliverability performance
    • Manage SPF, DKIM, DNS, suppression lists, and email authentication configurations
    • Ensure campaigns remain compliant with CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CCPA, and email marketing best practices
    • Troubleshoot deliverability issues using tools such as Litmus, GlockApps, or Postmark

Performance Optimization & Reporting

  • Conduct A/B testing on subject lines, CTAs, send times, layouts, and messaging
    • Analyze campaign performance metrics including open rates, CTR, conversion rates, bounce rates, and unsubscribe rates
    • Build dashboards and reports using Google Analytics, CRM platforms, Looker, or ESP analytics tools
    • Present findings, recommendations, and optimization strategies to leadership and stakeholders

What Makes You a Perfect Fit

  • Strong balance between creative marketing and analytical thinking
    • Excellent copywriting and communication skills with attention to detail
    • Technically capable of managing ESP configurations and deliverability troubleshooting
    • Organized and able to manage multiple campaigns, automations, and reporting cycles simultaneously
    • Data-driven mindset focused on continuous optimization and measurable results

Required Experience & Skills

  • 2+ years of professional email marketing experience
    • Hands-on experience with at least one major ESP (HubSpot, Klaviyo, Marketo, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign)
    • Strong understanding of audience segmentation and email automation workflows
    • Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, reporting, segmentation)
    • Basic HTML/CSS knowledge for email template customization
    • Experience tracking and analyzing email campaign performance metrics

Preferred Experience & Skills

  • Experience managing email programs for 50k+ contacts
    • Familiarity with deliverability and inbox placement tools (Litmus, GlockApps, Postmark)
    • Experience integrating ESPs with CRM systems such as Salesforce or HubSpot
    • Background in SaaS, e-commerce, or professional services industries
    • Understanding of lifecycle marketing and behavioral email strategies

What Does a Typical Day Look Like?

An Email Marketing Specialist’s day revolves around creating, launching, and optimizing campaigns that drive measurable engagement and revenue. You will:

  • Build and schedule campaigns while writing compelling copy and designing templates
    • Segment audiences to improve targeting and personalization
    • Monitor deliverability and maintain clean, healthy email databases
    • Launch and optimize automated nurture workflows and engagement sequences
    • Review analytics dashboards and conduct A/B testing to improve performance
    • Prepare reports and communicate campaign insights to marketing and leadership teams

In essence: you ensure email marketing campaigns are strategic, technically optimized, compliant, and consistently driving engagement, conversions, and revenue growth.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • Open rates meeting or exceeding industry benchmarks (20–40%)

• Click-through rates (CTR) ≥ 3–5%

  • Improved conversion rates across campaigns and workflows
    • Bounce rate maintained below 2% and unsubscribe rate below 1%
    • Accurate revenue attribution and reporting from email campaigns
    • Increased engagement, retention, and lead nurturing effectiveness

Interview Process

  • Initial Phone Screen

• Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter

  • Practical Assessment (e.g., build a 3-email nurture workflow in HubSpot for a sample product launch)
    • Client Interview

• Offer & Background Verification

About the company

Turning marketing into a market-domination weapon, we created a new category — the marketplace for future customers. Businesses shop for leads as they shop for products in e-commerce: you see everything about a lead before you buy — full transparency, control, and predictable outcomes. We're the #1 lead marketplace in the USA, and we're accelerating.

Role overview

We're looking for a Provider Manager to own the performance of our provider network — the core supply engine of the business. You manage existing providers, hunt and onboard new ones, and hold every partner accountable to quality, volume, and consistency. Your success is measured in revenue impact, not relationships maintained.

Supply is the business. If providers underperform, the marketplace stalls — and that's on you to prevent, not report on.

Requirements:

2+ years managing vendors, affiliates, partners, or external performance-based relationships — with revenue on the line.

Proven track record holding external partners accountable to hard quality and delivery standards, not just checking in.

Experience sourcing, evaluating, negotiating, and onboarding external partners end-to-end.

Data-driven by default — you make decisions from performance dashboards, not gut feel or vendor excuses.

Highly organized — can run 50+ active provider relationships without losing signal on any of them.

English C1+; you communicate with US-based providers daily and every message must be sharp and clear.

AI-first by default — if you are not already using AI to 3x your sourcing, monitoring, and communication output, you will be behind.

High ownership and strong decision-making in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

What You'll Be Doing:

Own the full provider lifecycle — sourcing, onboarding, performance management, and offboarding — no handoffs.

Monitor provider performance daily across lead quality, volume, conversion rates, and refund rates, and act before drops hit revenue.

Identify quality issues and delivery drops early with evidence, and drive them to resolution — not escalate them.

Push providers to improve output and marketplace fit; kill underperformers publicly instead of carrying them.

Build and maintain a live pipeline of new providers so supply grows continuously and no single provider can hold the marketplace hostage.

Reduce concentration risk by expanding and diversifying the provider network on a rolling basis.

Negotiate terms, payouts, and SLAs that align provider incentives with marketplace outcomes.

Collaborate tightly with client-facing, product, and ops teams to match provider output to real demand.

Track competitor supply moves and know where providers are being poached from or to before it shows up in your numbers.

This is not for you if

You manage partners by vibes and check-ins instead of metrics.

You avoid hard conversations and let underperformers coast.

You wait for dashboards to be built for you instead of digging into the data yourself.

You've only ever managed a handful of vendors and call it "partnerships."

You want a stable book of accounts to maintain — this role is about growing and cutting supply constantly.

You want the playbook handed to you — building it is the job.

What we expect from you (first 3 months)

We don't do long onboarding: access on day one, context in days, provider conversations in week one.

End of week 1: you have audited the current provider network, met the top 10 providers, and identified the 5 biggest risks to supply quality or volume with evidence.

End of month 1: you have onboarded your first new providers, taken action on at least 2 underperformers, and stood up a live performance view covering quality, volume, conversion, and refunds across the network.

End of quarter 1 (the bar): the network is measurably more diversified, at least one concentration risk is eliminated, underperformers have been cut or turned around, and net supply quality and volume are up on your watch.

Experience in real estate, lead generation, or marketplace businesses.

Familiarity with performance-based payouts, rev-share, or CPA/CPL models.

Background in affiliate management or supply-side operations.

Experience building or scaling vendor/provider operations from scratch.

Comfort with SQL, BI tools, or lightweight data work to interrogate provider performance yourself.

What We Offer:

Impact: Own the supply engine of a product-led, AI-powered marketplace where your decisions directly move revenue.

jobs.description:
Overview

Please note that while this is a remote role, this hire must reside in Mexico.

About HealthEdge

HealthEdge is a leading healthcare SaaS company delivering modern, cloud-native solutions that transform how health plans operate. With a global workforce spanning the US, India, Philippines, Mexico, and the UK, our Business Technology team powers the tools and platforms that keep HealthEdge running at scale – and Atlassian is at the center of how work gets done across the organization.

Role Overview

The Atlassian Administrator is a hands-on platform administration role responsible for the day-to-day configuration, maintenance, and user support of HealthEdge's Atlassian environment, including Jira Software, Jira Service Management (JSM), and Confluence. Working within the Atlassian Products team and reporting to the Manager, Atlassian Products, you will be a key execution resource for platform requests, project configuration, user management, and basic automation – ensuring that thousands of users across the organization can work effectively in Atlassian tools every day.

This is a great role for someone with solid Atlassian fundamentals who wants to deepen their platform expertise in a complex, high-scale environment. You'll work closely with Senior Atlassian Administrators, Architects, and the team manager, taking on well-defined configuration tasks and growing toward more advanced solution design and automation work over time. As HealthEdge moves fully to Atlassian Cloud Enterprise, this role will grow to include working with AI-native features like Atlassian Intelligence and Rovo — making content governance and platform hygiene directly connected to AI quality.

What You'll Do

Platform Administration & Configuration

  • Administer Jira Software, Jira Service Management, and Confluence in a cloud environment
  • Create and maintain Jira projects, boards, workflows, permission schemes, notification schemes, and screens under the guidance of senior team members
  • Configure and manage JSM service desk projects including request types, queues, SLA configurations, and portal settings
  • Manage Confluence spaces, page permissions, templates, and basic macros to support team knowledge management
  • Perform user and group management including account creation, license assignments, group membership, and access reviews
  • Process and fulfill Atlassian support requests from end users, maintaining SLA compliance in the team's JSM queue

Automation & Reporting

  • Build and maintain native Jira and JSM automation rules for common workflows – ticket routing, notifications, field updates, and status transitions
  • Create and maintain dashboards, saved filters, and basic reports to support team and stakeholder visibility
  • Assist with Confluence automation and page template maintenance
  • Support testing and rollout of automation changes developed by Senior Administrators

User Support & Enablement

  • Serve as a first point of contact for Atlassian support requests, resolving common configuration and usage questions
  • Escalate complex or high-impact issues to Senior Atlassian Administrators with clear documentation and context
  • Assist in onboarding new users and teams to Atlassian tools, including basic training and guidance on project setup
  • Contribute to and maintain Atlassian knowledge base articles and how-to documentation for end users

Governance & Housekeeping

  • Perform routine platform hygiene tasks including inactive user cleanup, stale project reviews, and unused field or scheme audits
  • Assist with license usage tracking and reporting to support renewal planning
  • Follow and help enforce Atlassian governance standards for project naming, permissions, and configuration consistency
  • Support audit and compliance activities related to Atlassian access and configuration

Project & Team Support

  • Assist Senior Administrators and the team manager with larger configuration projects, migrations, and platform improvement initiatives
  • Participate in testing and validation of Atlassian upgrades, app changes, and configuration rollouts
  • Document changes accurately in accordance with team change management practices

What You'll Bring

Required

  • 2–4 years of hands-on Jira and Confluence administration experience in a corporate environment
  • Working knowledge of Jira Software project types, workflows, permission schemes, and issue configuration
  • Experience configuring and supporting Jira Service Management (JSM) service desk projects
  • Familiarity with Confluence space administration, page permissions, and content organization
  • Experience with native Jira automation rules
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills – platform hygiene and accuracy matter in this role
  • Good written and verbal English communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent requests and prioritize effectively
  • Familiarity with Atlassian Marketplace apps (ScriptRunner, Elements Connect, or similar)
  • Familiarity with Atlassian Intelligence or Rovo
  • Exposure to ITIL frameworks or service management best practices
  • Experience working with Atlassian Cloud (vs. Data Center/Server only)

Preferred

  • Atlassian certification (ACP-120 Jira Administration or equivalent)
  • Experience working in a global, multi-time zone organization

What Success Looks Like

Within 90 days, you are independently handling the majority of day-to-day Atlassian support requests, have a solid working knowledge of HealthEdge's project and space structure, and are contributing to platform hygiene initiatives. Within six months, you are building and maintaining automation rules confidently, your queue work is consistently within SLA, and stakeholders are getting reliable, well-configured solutions from you. Within a year, you have grown your platform depth meaningfully, are contributing to larger configuration projects, and are beginning to take on more complex solution design work with senior team support.

About the Team

You'll join a dedicated Atlassian Products team within Business Technology, focused on making Jira, JSM, and Confluence work well for thousands of users across a complex global organization. The team values platform rigor, clean governance, and user-focused solutions – and invests in growing the skills of everyone on it. This role is an excellent entry point into a team where strong administrators can grow into senior and lead positions over time.

Geographic Responsibility: Remote, Mexico

Type of Employment: Full-time, permanent

Work Environment: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job: 

  • The employee is occasionally required to move around the office. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Work across multiple time zones in a hybrid or remote work environment.
  • Long periods of time sitting and/or standing in front of a computer using video technology.
  • May require travel dependent on company needs.

jobs.description:
Senior Cost Estimator (SCE)

Remote | Hybrid option: Melbourne, FL or Ellicott City, MD

Salary Range: $125,000-$150,000

The Role

Above Group is looking for a Senior Cost Estimator to own cost estimating on our design projects, from conceptual budgeting through construction documents. You will serve as lead estimator on assigned projects and be the person engineers, project managers, and clients turn to when a design decision has a dollar figure attached. Our portfolio leans heavily toward government and healthcare work, where estimates must be accurate, defensible, and tied tightly to scope.

This is a senior role with real latitude. You will build and maintain the department’s master unit-cost database and historical cost library, set the standards and templates the team estimates by, and directly influence which projects we pursue and how we price them.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop and manage cost estimates for multi-disciplinary projects at every design phase, conceptual, schematic, design development, and construction documents, and own their accuracy and consistency; serving as lead estimator on assigned projects
  • Perform quantity takeoffs directly from Revit and AutoCAD models alongside our BIM and design teams
  • Resolve gaps between design intent, scope, and budget through value engineering and cost-benefit analysis
  • Prepare conceptual budgets, fee proposals, and comparative cost models supporting business development for prospective clients and projects
  • Write basis-of-estimate (BOE) narratives, cost reports, scope clarifications, and qualifications/exclusions; respond to RFIs
  • Build and maintain the department’s unit-cost database, historical cost library, and estimating standards
  • Keep estimates current with code requirements, jurisdictional fees, local bidding conditions, labor rates, and material pricing
  • Review design concepts with engineering leads and project managers to align design intent with project budgets

What you Bring to the Role

  • 6–10 years in cost estimating, general contracting, or related construction work (or an equivalent combination of education and experience)
  • Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent field/trade experience considered
  • General contracting background strongly preferred, with hands-on field and/or estimating experience
  • Estimating experience in the government and healthcare markets strongly preferred
  • Experience benchmarking labor and material costs against historical data, vendor quotes, and subcontractor pricing.
  • Working knowledge of estimating platforms (RSMeans, Sage Estimating/Accubid, ConEst, WinEst, Trade Service) and takeoff tools (Bluebeam Revu, On-Screen Takeoff, or similar)
  • Enough Revit and AutoCAD to extract quantities and review MEP design documents
  • Proficient knowledge of computers and Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Word); Advanced Excel: pivot tables, formulas, macros
  • Familiarity with mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, telecommunications, and fire protection systems as they relate to cost, constructability, and market pricing
  • Strong understanding of general contracting practices, bid processes, subcontractor scope leveling, and contractor cost coding (CSI MasterFormat)
  • Strong written and verbal communication; you can hold your own with clients, contractors, and senior leadership
  • Ability to work independently/self-motivated, as well as in a collaborative team setting, highly organized, and detail oriented
  • Impactful analytical, strategic planning, with the ability to manage multiple estimates and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Discretion and dependability with sensitive cost and client information
  • S. citizenship or U.S. permanent residency
  • Willingness to travel up to 20% for site visits and client meetings

Nice to have: ASPE Certified Professional Estimator (CPE), AACE Certified Estimating Professional (CEP), or similar certification.

Why Above Group

We are a faith-based AEC firm built around a simple idea: continuously improving the built environment for the glory of God. Our mission is to demonstrate the love of Jesus Christ by empowering excellent AEC professionals to provide superior service. Four values guide how we work: Christian Values, Uncompromising Quality, Buffalo (running toward challenges rather than away from them), and Extreme Team. If that resonates with you, you will fit here.

Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, life and disability coverage, employer-funded HSA contributions, and an annual profit-sharing bonus tied to the company’s collective results.

Remote Work Requirements

This role is fully remote or a hybrid option for candidates residing near Melbourne, FL or Ellicott City, MD. Any type of remote work requires reliable high-speed internet capable of supporting video conferencing, VPN, and cloud applications; a secure home network appropriate for confidential company and client information; and a dedicated, quiet workspace suitable for sustained focus and professional video meetings.

Salary: $125,000-$150,000

🤓 TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We've been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners — people with no prior tech background — through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.

We are seeking a data-driven and strategic Senior User Acquisition Manager to lead our Meta Ads efforts across the US region. Reporting to our Marketing Lead, you will be responsible for scaling high-budget campaigns and optimizing complex funnels to drive enrollment for our high-value tech programs.

What you will do

  • Own the budget and paid strategy for the advanced programs line — roughly $200K/month today, scaling several times over by year-end.
  • Run Meta and Google (YouTube included) as core volume channels; open LinkedIn and run experiments in Reddit and Twitter.
  • Own campaign and ad-set architecture, plus the keep-or-kill calls: small batches, a data threshold before deciding, weekly cadence, an honest decision log.
  • Brief the content producer and judge the output on metrics — you don't write scripts or build pages, creatives, or dashboards yourself.
  • Own traffic quality rather than cost per lead: read sales call transcripts, see who actually shows up, and influence target-audience share.
  • Own attribution and conversion events — pixel and event setup, separate buying infrastructure, and reconciling the ad account against CRM and BI.
  • Take each new program in the line into your channels with its own funnel and targets, adding sales rather than redistributing share.

  • 4+ years in performance marketing or user acquisition, with hands-on account work at real budgets in expensive markets in the last year or two.
  • You have experience with expensive acquisition and long, multi-step funnels — education, B2B, fintech, high-ticket services — in the last two to three years, not earlier in your resume.
  • Comfort with narrow audiences and thin data, where judgment fills the gap statistics won't, and a clear answer to what "enough delivery to decide" means.

Security Operations Engineer

About the Team

The Security Operations team plays a critical role in protecting CircleCI’s infrastructure, product, and customer data against an evolving threat landscape. From incident response to hardening our cloud and CI/CD environments, the team works closely with engineering to keep CircleCI secure, resilient, and ready for what’s next.

About the Role

As a Security Operations Engineer, you’ll play a key role in protecting CircleCI’s infrastructure, product, and customer data against an evolving threat landscape increasingly shaped by AI-driven attacks and AI-augmented defenses. This intermediate-level role offers the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of security challenges, work closely with Engineering as a trusted security partner, and expand your impact across the organization. You’ll contribute to our security roadmap while leveraging AI tooling to advance how we detect, respond to, and automate security threats across CircleCI.

What You’ll Do:

Threat Detection & Incident Response

  • Monitor, investigate, and respond to security threats across CircleCI’s cloud and application environments, using security and AI-assisted tooling to improve detection and triage.
  • Participate in security risk assessments, incident response, post-incident reviews, and rotating on-call support, turning findings into stronger controls and processes.

Security Engineering & Architecture

  • Build and maintain security tooling, controls, and automation across cloud, application, and CI/CD environments, following established security patterns and best practices.
  • Identify vulnerabilities and configuration risks, contribute to security runbooks and compliance requirements, and develop a growing understanding of CircleCI’s security architecture.

AI & Security

  • Incorporate AI-powered security tools into day-to-day workflows and help evaluate emerging technologies that can improve detection, response, and automation.
  • Stay current on AI-specific security threats and contribute to responsible approaches for using AI in security operations.

Cross-Team Partnership & Ownership

  • Partner with Engineering teams to understand security needs, provide practical guidance, and translate technical risks into clear, actionable recommendations.
  • Contribute to security roadmap planning, technology evaluations, and team documentation while building strong relationships across Security and Engineering.

What You’ll Bring:

  • 3+ years of security engineering or security operations experience, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud, application, and CI/CD security, ideally in AWS, GCP, or Azure environments.
  • Experience with security incident response and common security tooling, including EDR, CNAPP, SASE, vulnerability scanners, and log analysis.
  • Ability to build and maintain security automation and tooling, with experience in languages or technologies such as Go, Python, or Terraform.
  • Strong security judgment and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess risk, make recommendations, and take action when information is incomplete.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

This is a fully remote role supporting a team in the EST time zone (9 AM–5 PM EST). Hiring locations include Brazil and Portugal.

About the role

As we take on enterprise accounts and hire into service teams at pace, the systems that hold client delivery together are being rebuilt ad hoc by team leads in Google Sheets, outside Notion, and outside anyone's line of sight but the account lead's. We need to centralize workflow development and ensure teams are trained and supported in existing systems.

This Operations Specialist will operate across client operations: onboarding and offboarding; workflow refinement, maintenance, training, and client tailoring; compliance and usage across service teams.

Ongoing Responsibilities

1. Client Operations

  • Onboarding & offboarding. Own the operational backend for new and departing clients: kick-off and offboarding coordination, documentation and credential access, access revocation, and the integrity of our client databases throughout.

  • Client success support. Serve as the operational counterpart to account leads, keeping delivery infrastructure current as scopes, teams, and client needs change.

    • When an enterprise client signs, embed with that account and team through the first 30–60 days, when a newly assembled team is competent but not yet confident in our systems.

    • Tailor systems to the client. Build the views, dashboards, and structures a specific client needs inside our stack, so uniform solutions live in Notion and remain visible to leadership.

  • Staffing upkeep. Partner with Service Directors on staffing changes, capacity tracking, and the staffing ledger as restaffing, change orders, and offboardings arise.

2. Operational Platform Ownership

  • Proactive systems adoption. Assess day-over-day application of our systems by teams, and intervene before workarounds calcify.

  • Understand our service teams and operate as their operational partner, knowing their workflows better than anyone outside the team.

  • Audit and build workflows. When a team needs a new workflow, you scope it, assist building it, and own it rather than routing it back to them.

  • Compliance and training. Keep your teams trained on and compliant with the project management system, and own the escalation path when they are not.

  • Onboard new hires onto the project management system and into the operational rhythm of their team.

  • Platform support. Serve as a go-to for Notion troubleshooting, database hygiene, and structural questions across the agency.

3. Internal Operations

  • Automations. Build and maintain automations across the internal stack (Notion, Slack, Google Workspace, Fireflies, and our automation platform) that remove manual work.

  • Documentation. Write SOPs and training material for what you build, so processes run without you in the room.

  • Operational initiatives. Contribute to company-wide operational projects alongside the Director of Operations and peers within the team.

Growth Path

This role is part of a specialized Operations track. As Operations scales, Specialists grow into Operations Leads who own a defined segment of the business and are directly responsible for the specialized workflows and tooling that segment runs on.

Core Competencies

Must-Have: Hard Skills

  • Experience in a client-facing operations, account management, or project management role, ideally at an agency or with DTC / e-commerce brands.

  • Applied experience using AI tools to improve operational speed and output quality.

  • Professional-level competency in Notion: databases, relations, rollups, views, permissions, and the judgment to know when a structure is wrong.

  • Hands-on experience building automations end to end (Zapier, Make, n8n, or similar), including API-based integrations across SaaS tools.

  • Strong communication in English, written and verbal: SOPs, training material, and async updates people actually follow, plus the confidence to present to executive stakeholders.

Must-Have: Soft Skills

  • Ownership instinct. Takes a problem end to end without waiting to be assigned it, and treats what they build as theirs to maintain rather than hand off. Resourceful and autonomous; prefers ownership to supervision.

  • Growth mentality. Wants the role to outgrow its current shape, seeks feedback directly, and takes on scope slightly before being ready for it.

  • Exceptionally organized, with the attention to detail to catch what others miss before it reaches a client.

  • Energized by new tools and technology. Picks up unfamiliar platforms fast and enjoys building systems in them rather than waiting to be trained on them.

  • Comfortable holding peers to a standard without escalating every time.

Nice-to-Have

  • Familiarity with agency service models across paid media, creative, retention, or marketplaces.

  • Experience supporting enterprise accounts through onboarding.

  • Background in process documentation, SOP libraries, or knowledge management.

Working at Darkroom

Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics.

  • Unlimited PTO + Local holidays (Relevant to your hub): Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp.

  • Remote-First Culture: Many roles are fully remote. Employees based in or near our New York or Lisbon HQs are expected to work hybrid with weekly in-office time. Hub locations include the Brazil and Spain.

  • Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition.

  • Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry.

Equal Opportunity Statement

Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

jobs.excerpt: Was wir suchenDie #1 Plattform für NeukundenJedes Unternehmen braucht laufend neue Kunden – und genau dieses Problem lösen wir.
jobs.description:
Was wir suchen

Die #1 Plattform für Neukunden

Jedes Unternehmen braucht laufend neue Kunden – und genau dieses Problem lösen wir. Mit Interlead bauen wir die #1 Plattform für Leads, Termine und Aufträge und machen die Kundengewinnung für unsere Partner damit einfacher, transparenter und planbarer.

Zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt suchen wir daher einen Head of Engineering (m/w/d) für unser IT Team, zu 100 % aus dem Home-Office (Deutschland) oder bei uns im Bremer Office!

Das sind deine Aufgaben

  • Du führst unser Tech-Team (aktuell 8 Personen aus Entwicklung, Daten und Infrastruktur) disziplinarisch und fachlich – inklusive 1:1s, Zielvereinbarungen, Weiterentwicklung und Recruiting neuer Teammitglieder.
  • Du übernimmst das operative Tagesgeschäft des CTO: Priorisierung, Ressourcenplanung, Eskalationen und alle Entscheidungen, die heute noch an ihm hängen bleiben.
  • Du verantwortest die Umsetzung unserer Roadmap über alle vier Bereiche hinweg – Product, Daten, Software und Infrastruktur – und sorgst dafür, dass zugesagte Termine gehalten werden.
  • Du sorgst für planbare Lieferfähigkeit: Du etablierst klare Prozesse für Planung, Entwicklung, Testing und Release und machst den Fortschritt für alle Bereiche im Unternehmen sichtbar.
  • Du baust eine belastbare Datenbasis auf: Du bringst unsere Kennzahlen zu Leads, Terminen und Aufträgen in eine Form, der Sales, Marketing und Geschäftsführung vertrauen können.
  • Du verantwortest Stabilität, Security und Skalierbarkeit unserer Plattform – von Monitoring und Incident-Management über Backups und Zugriffsrechte bis zu DSGVO-Themen.
  • Du bleibst technisch nah dran: Du bewertest Architekturentscheidungen, liest Code-Reviews mit und kannst im Zweifel selbst in den Code schauen – auch wenn du nicht mehr die Mehrheit deiner Zeit dort verbringst.
  • Du steuerst technische Schulden aktiv: Du machst sie sichtbar, bewertest sie wirtschaftlich und verhandelst mit den Fachbereichen, wann wir sie abbauen.
  • Du bist der Ansprechpartner der Fachbereiche für alle technischen Themen und übersetzt zwischen Business-Anforderung und technischer Umsetzung.
  • Du steuerst externe Dienstleister und Tools, inklusive Auswahl, Verträgen und Budgetverantwortung für den IT-Bereich.

Dank deiner Expertise erreichst du folgende Meilensteine bei uns

  • 0-3 Monate:

    • Du kennst Team, Systemlandschaft, Roadmap und die wichtigsten Stakeholder und hast mit jedem Teammitglied ein 1:1 geführt
    • Du hast eine schriftliche Bestandsaufnahme erstellt: größte Risiken in Stabilität und Security, größte Engpässe in der Lieferfähigkeit, Zustand unserer Datenbasis
    • Du hast die 1:1s, die operative Priorisierung und die täglichen Eskalationen vollständig vom CTO übernommen
    • Gemeinsam mit dem CTO ist schriftlich festgehalten, welche Entscheidungen bei dir liegen und welche bei ihm

  • 4-6 Monate:

    • Fachbereiche wissen jederzeit, woran gearbeitet wird
    • Monitoring, Alerting und ein Incident-Prozess inklusive Post-Mortems sind etabliert; kritische Security- und DSGVO-Lücken aus der Bestandsaufnahme sind geschlossen
    • Eine erste verlässliche Version unseres Kennzahlen-Reportings zu Leads, Terminen und Aufträgen ist live – mit klar definierten Metriken und benannten Ownern
    • Der CTO wird nur noch bei strategischen Fragen eingebunden, nicht mehr im Tagesgeschäft

  • 7-12 Monate:

    • Die Lieferfähigkeit ist messbar besser als bei deinem Start (z. B. kürzere Durchlaufzeiten, höhere Release-Frequenz, weniger Fehler in Produktion)
    • Ein Plan zum Abbau technischer Schulden läuft und ist mit den Fachbereichen abgestimmt
    • Das Team ist entsprechend der Wachstumsplanung aufgestockt und strukturiert; du hast selbst eingestellt und Verantwortung im Team weiterverteilt
    • Die Plattform trägt das geplante Wachstum ohne Stabilitätsprobleme, und die Datenbasis ist im Unternehmen die anerkannte Wahrheit

Das bringst du mit

  • Mindestens 2 Jahre Erfahrung in der Führung von Tech-Teams (ab ca. 3 Personen) – als Head of Engineering, Engineering Manager, Teamlead, Head of Engineering oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle
  • Einen soliden technischen Hintergrund als Entwicklerin oder Entwickler (idealerweise 5+ Jahre) – du hast selbst gebaut, was du heute verantwortest
  • Verantwortung über mehrere Disziplinenhinweg: Du hast nicht nur Entwicklung geführt, sondern auch mit Daten und/oder Infrastruktur zu tun gehabt
  • Praktische Erfahrung mit Cloud-Infrastruktur (AWS, GCP oder Azure), CI/CD und modernen Web- und Plattform-Architekturen
  • Ein sicheres Gefühl für Priorisierung: Du kannst begründet Nein sagen und hältst auch dann Kurs, wenn mehrere Bereiche gleichzeitig etwas von dir wollen
  • Erfahrung darin, Prozesse einzuführen, die tatsächlich gelebt werden – ohne das Team in Bürokratie zu ersticken
  • Ein datengetriebener Arbeitsstil: Du misst, bevor du entscheidest, und machst Ergebnisse für andere nachvollziehbar
  • Kommunikationsstärke Richtung Nicht-Techniker: Du kannst Sales, Marketing und Geschäftsführung erklären, warum etwas dauert – so, dass es verstanden und akzeptiert wird
  • Eigenverantwortung und Umsetzungsstärke: Du wartest nicht auf Aufträge, sondern erkennst selbst, was zu tun ist
  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (mind. C1) und gute Englischkenntnisse
  • Erfahrung in einem schnell wachsenden Umfeld (Start-up, Scale-up oder Agentur) ist ein klarer Pluspunkt
  • Erfahrung mit Lead-Generierung, Performance Marketing oder B2B-SaaS ist ein Bonus, aber keine Voraussetzung

Was uns wichtig ist

  • Diese Stelle kann zu 100 % im Home Office erledigt werden. Für Team-Events und Quartalsplanung freuen wir uns über ca. 1–2 Präsenztage pro Quartal in unserem Headquarter in der Bremer Überseestadt (Reisekosten übernehmen wir).
  • Du berichtest direkt an den CTO und bist Teil des erweiterten Führungskreises.
  • Es handelt sich um eine Vollzeitstelle in unbefristeter Anstellung.
  • Diese Rolle ist bewusst breit angelegt: Product, Daten, Software und Infrastruktur laufen bei dir zusammen.

Das bieten wir dir

  • Ein dynamisches Marketing- und Tech-Umfeld sowie die Möglichkeit, gemeinsam “The Lead Company” aufzubauen.
  • Ein riesiger Markt und zahlreiche interne Wachstumsmöglichkeiten – wir lösen das größte Problem unserer Partner: die Automatisierung ihrer Neukundengewinnung.
  • Volle Flexibilität im Arbeitsort (remote, im Bremer Headquarter oder nach Absprache auch aus dem Ausland).
  • Volle Flexibilität in der Arbeitszeit – du gestaltest deine Arbeitszeiten individuell mit deinem Team.
  • 30 Tage Urlaub pro Jahr + die Möglichkeit, jederzeit unbezahlten Urlaub zu nehmen.
  • Zuschuss zur betrieblichen Altersvorsorge (die “Interlead‑Rente”).
  • Jährliche Teamevents wie Sommerfest & Weihnachtsfeier.
  • Agiles Arbeitsumfeld – moderne Tools wie Slack, Monday, Notion, Google Workspace und OKRs/Scrum unterstützen dich bei der täglichen Arbeit.
  • Zuschuss fürs Fitnessstudio (über Urban Sports Club oder E‑Gym Wellpass).
  • Schnelle Entscheidungen – wir sind 100 % bootstrapped, profitabel und unabhängig von Investoren.
  • Eine offene Feedback‑Kultur und regelmäßige interne Trainings.
  • Transparente Kommunikation durch monatliche All‑Hands‑Meetings, wöchentlichen Newsletter und feste Team‑Updates.
  • Im Headquarter in der Bremer Überseestadt erwarten dich ergonomische Arbeitsplätze, großartiger Kaffee & Espresso, Getränke und Grillabende.
  • Für Home‑Office‑Mitarbeitende: monatliche Home‑Office‑Pauschale von 20 €.
  • Bikeleasing, lease dein Wunschfahrrad oder E-Bike zu attraktiven Konditionen.

Das sind unsere Werte

  • Fail Fast: Wir leben eine ausgeprägte Testing- und Fehlerkultur. Wir sind pragmatisch, mutig und fühlen uns mit Veränderung wohl.
  • Ergebnisse: Wir arbeiten flexibel, aber verlässlich. Bei uns steht Freiheit in Einklang mit Ergebnisorientierung und Eigenverantwortung.
  • Vertrauen: Wir gehen offen mit Zahlen, Stärken und Schwächen um und machen das, was für die Firma richtig ist ("Ego zurück").

jobs.description:
Head of Academy
Reporting Line

Reports to the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO) for day-to-day operations, with a dotted line to the CEO for commercial outcomes. The CHRO at this organisation is a commercial role with direct accountability for business outcomes — not a back-office function.

No direct reports at this stage — the role operates as a solo lead, leveraging AI tooling in place of traditional headcount.

Location

Remote (European timezone preferred). Occasional travel to group sales offices to engage with introducing brokers and understand client needs firsthand.

General Purpose

The Head of Academy builds and runs the group's AI-first online learning platform, serving two audiences with equal weight: helping traders develop the skills that keep them engaged and active, and equipping introducing brokers with the knowledge and tools to grow their client base and generate more business.

Specific Objectives

Launch the AI-personalised learning engine

Ship a working version of the personalised curriculum system — integrating with a trading analytics engine (Tradefora or equivalent) — so that course selection is driven by trader profile, stated goals, and actual trading behaviour, not manual browsing. Live within the first 90 days.

Drive measurable trader retention

Achieve a 10% improvement in trader retention attributable to Academy engagement, measured at 12 months against a pre-launch baseline. Trader engagement metrics — course completions, return logins, active learning sessions — serve as the leading indicators.

Build and measure IB development

Deliver a dedicated IB learning and content track — including edutainment and branded content designed to acquire as well as educate — with success measured by CRM-attributed trader acquisition. The target: participating IBs show a 10% uplift in new trader acquisition attributable to Academy-produced content within 12 months. Content consumption and distribution serve as supporting diagnostics.

Map the full trader journey

Document and partially build the end-to-end "Zero to Hero" pathway — from onboarding a new trader through to live trading, strategy codification, and agentic trading compatibility with MT5 and TradingView.

Convert IBs from non-exclusive to exclusive

Achieve a 20% increase in exclusive partnership agreements among Academy-engaged IBs within 12 months, driven by the tangible value the Academy delivers to their business.


Key Activities

Nothing exists yet — no platform, no content, no stack, no team. What follows is what building it from zero actually looks like.

Design and run AI-powered content workflows

Commission, quality-check, and iterate trading and IB education content using AI tooling — treating large language models and specialist AI agents as the primary content engine, with the role focused on prompt engineering, curation, and continuous improvement. This includes edutainment and branded content designed to acquire as well as educate.

Build and manage the personalisation layer

Connect trading data sources (including Tradefora or equivalent analytics integrations) to the learning platform via API, and configure AI-driven logic that matches each trader's profile, goals, and behavioural data to the right curriculum path.

Select and orchestrate the technology stack

Evaluate, choose, and integrate the platform, AI agents, and automation tools needed to run the Academy — remaining platform-agnostic and replacing traditional headcount with agent-based workflows wherever possible.

Own the IB learning track

Design and maintain a dedicated curriculum for introducing brokers, drawing on direct engagement with sales offices to understand what IBs actually need to grow their client base and onboard active traders.

Monitor performance and iterate

Track retention, engagement, and learning outcomes across both trader and IB audiences; use data to identify gaps, retire underperforming content, and prioritise the next build cycle.


Key Competences

AI tooling fluency

Proven ability to build workflows using LLMs, AI agents, and automation tools — not just as a user but as an orchestrator who can replace traditional headcount with agent-based processes.

AI-driven content creation

Able to use AI to research, write, structure, and iterate educational content at scale — comfortable with prompt engineering, output curation, and quality control without relying on human subject matter experts.

API integration and data literacy

Comfortable connecting platforms and data sources via API, and using trading or behavioural data to drive personalisation logic — no deep engineering required, but enough to own the integration decisions.

Solo operator mindset

Able to build, run, and iterate a multi-audience product without a team — self-directing, bias to action, comfortable with ambiguity in an early-stage environment.

Trading and financial markets knowledge

Sufficient understanding of retail trading, broker ecosystems, and the IB model to commission credible content and engage meaningfully with traders and IBs. An AI-native candidate is expected to close any gaps here quickly on the job.

Learning design awareness

A working grasp of curriculum structure and learner journeys — not a prerequisite, but something an AI-native candidate is expected to develop quickly on the job.


Likely Current Job

AI Automation Specialist / AI Workflow Builder

Someone currently building agent-based workflows and LLM-powered products — the closest direct match to how this role actually operates day-to-day.

Solo EdTech Builder / Online Course Creator

An independent operator who has built and monetised an online learning product, ideally using AI tooling to create and deliver content at scale.

Growth Hacker / No-Code Product Builder

Someone who has launched and iterated a digital product solo — comfortable with APIs, automation platforms, and a bias-to-action approach in an early-stage environment.

Digital Marketing Automation Lead

A marketer who has moved into AI-driven workflows — content at scale, personalisation logic, behavioural data — and is ready to own a product rather than a campaign.

Fintech or Trading Platform Product Manager

Someone with enough financial markets exposure to engage credibly with traders and IBs, who has pivoted toward AI-native ways of working.

Employer Value Proposition

You inherit an existing base of active traders and introducing brokers on day one — then build the Academy that monetises it. No cold-start problem, no fundraising, no co-founder risk: the distribution is already there, and your job is to build the engine that turns it into a business.

The hard part is real and worth naming: there is no platform, no content, no stack, and no team. You are building a product, a tech stack, a content engine, and a business model simultaneously — from a blank page. That's either the most exciting brief you've ever seen or the wrong role entirely. The right candidate will know which.

What makes it worth it: you are the Academy — sole decision-maker on strategy, stack, content, and growth — backed by the infrastructure, client base, and active support of a large multinational broker that has committed to making this work. The organisation is behind you. The starting conditions are genuinely favourable.

The financial upside is real and direct: profit share tied to the incremental business the Academy generates. The better you build it, the more you earn from it.

The starting model is lean and AI-first — you operate solo, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting. If the business grows to warrant it, so does the team. You shape what that looks like.

This role is for someone who has already built something meaningful with AI — and is done doing it for someone else's upside.

Compensation

Base salary plus performance bonus. The bonus is tied to two primary revenue streams: incremental trader retention and IB business development. Educational services sales forms a third stream but is not a focus metric at this stage.

Assessment Process

Candidates meet first with the CHRO, then with the CEO. Shortlisted candidates are asked to prepare a brief business plan and live demo — showing how they would approach building the Academy, including the AI tooling and workflows they'd put to work.

Overview

LMI is seeking a Senior Project Manager to support a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) program focused on suicide prevention and mental health. This role will lead technical projects and workstreams across a multidisciplinary program involving digital solutions, Microsoft Power Platform, SharePoint, analytics, data, and program evaluation.

The successful candidate will serve as the primary owner for assigned projects—translating client needs into actionable technical requirements, coordinating delivery teams, managing scope and priorities, and ensuring solutions are delivered successfully. This individual should be comfortable working directly with developers, analysts, data scientists, evaluators, and business stakeholders and have enough technical fluency to understand dependencies, challenge assumptions, identify risks, and drive decisions.

This role is well suited for a strong project leader who wants to deepen their technical delivery experience while developing toward broader program management responsibilities. Prior VA experience is a significant plus.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and intelligence sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

  • Own the planning, execution, and delivery of assigned technical projects and workstreams from requirements through implementation.
  • Serve as the primary point of coordination between VA stakeholders, program leadership, and technical delivery teams.
  • Translate ambiguous or evolving client needs into clear technical requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, delivery plans, and priorities.
  • Lead delivery using Scrum, Kanban, or hybrid Agile approaches, including backlog management, sprint planning, prioritization, reviews, retrospectives, and dependency management.
  • Manage work in Jira, Azure DevOps, SharePoint, and related delivery tools, maintaining clear visibility into status, risks, blockers, dependencies, and decisions.
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary teams that may include Power Platform developers, SharePoint developers, software developers, data scientists, analysts, evaluators, and subject matter experts.
  • Partner with technical leads to understand solution approaches, architecture, data dependencies, integration points, security considerations, and implementation risks.
  • Drive technical delivery by identifying blockers, resolving cross-team dependencies, escalating issues when appropriate, and ensuring teams remain focused on defined outcomes.
  • Manage project scope, schedule, resources, milestones, and performance while proactively addressing risks and changing priorities.
  • Lead requirements-gathering sessions, technical discussions, demonstrations, client reviews, and project status meetings.
  • Develop and maintain project documentation, roadmaps, delivery plans, decision logs, dashboards, and client-facing briefings.
  • Ensure technical deliverables meet client requirements, acceptance criteria, quality expectations, and applicable VA standards.
  • Support projects involving Microsoft Power Platform, SharePoint modernization, workflow automation, analytics, data visualization, and program evaluation.
  • Partner with analysts and evaluators to ensure technical solutions effectively support program measurement, operational decision-making, and client objectives.
  • Identify opportunities to improve development processes, Agile practices, technical delivery, documentation, and team collaboration.
  • Support release planning, testing, user acceptance, implementation, and transition activities as appropriate.
  • Build trusted relationships with VA clients by communicating technical concepts, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations in clear business language.
  • Support program leadership with staffing, resource planning, risk management, forecasting, and broader contract execution.
  • Contribute to solutioning, business development, proposals, and account growth by identifying client needs and helping shape technically informed approaches.
  • Take on increasing program-level responsibilities as experience and program needs evolve.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, engineering, data analytics, business, management, public health, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in project management, technology consulting, digital delivery, systems implementation, federal contracting, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience independently owning technical projects or complex workstreams through the full delivery lifecycle.
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams that include technical and non-technical personnel.
  • Strong working knowledge of Agile methodologies, including Scrum, Kanban, or hybrid delivery approaches.
  • Hands-on experience using Jira, Azure DevOps, or comparable tools to manage backlogs, requirements, dependencies, and delivery.
  • Technical familiarity with one or more of the following:
    • Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power BI, or Power Automate;
    • SharePoint development, modernization, or workflow solutions;
    • Data analytics, visualization, or data-driven applications;
    • Program evaluation or performance measurement solutions.
  • Ability to translate business and program needs into clear technical requirements and actionable delivery plans.
  • Ability to understand and communicate technical concepts, solution tradeoffs, dependencies, and risks to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong operational, organizational, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, take ownership, and drive delivery with limited direction.
  • Excellent client-facing communication, facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt quickly to changing client needs.

  • Experience supporting technical solutioning, business development, capture, or proposal development.
  • Demonstrated interest in progressing into a Program Manager or Deputy Program Manager role.
