jobs.description:
About the Role

Popmenu is hiring its first GTM Engineer to build the systems that power our go-to-market motion. This is a build role. You will design those systems from the ground up and have real latitude in deciding what gets built first.

We run a high-velocity, low-ACV motion: thousands of addressable restaurants in every market we sell into, and a sales cycle typically under 30 days. Our Sales, Marketing and CX teams run well on processes they have built and refined themselves. What they do not have yet are the systems to take that repetitive work off them, orchestrate the handoffs between them, and put the right accounts in front of the right person automatically. Building those systems is how we intend to have the sharpest, most efficient go-to-market motion in restaurant technology.

You will report to our Chief Business Officer and Co-Founder and work across Sales, Marketing and CX. Salesforce and Salesloft are our system of record and sequencing today, and the data, enrichment and automation around them is largely yours to build. Nobody hands you a backlog here. You will find where we are losing hours and where we are losing accounts, decide what matters most, and build the fix.

What You'll Own

Pipeline and Targeting

  • A single source of truth for every addressable restaurant in our markets, US and UK, assigned to territory automatically, enriched, and scored on fit and intent
  • An AI-native outbound engine that turns cold restaurants into booked conversations, at a volume no team could run manually
  • The infrastructure that makes that volume possible: domain strategy, inbox rotation, warmup and sender reputation
  • Inbound speed to lead, plus routing and attribution in partnership with Marketing

Sales Productivity

  • Take the repetitive work off our AEs: list building, account research, call prep, follow-up, routing and data entry
  • Put reps in front of prioritized, signal-ranked queues instead of a blank search bar

CX and Post-Sale Efficiency

  • Bring the same leverage to onboarding, support workflows and account health scoring
  • Orchestrate the handoffs between Sales, Marketing and CX so nothing is rekeyed, re-researched or dropped between teams
  • Automate the good processes that are still being run manually, without breaking what already works

Systems, Stack and Roadmap

  • Own the architecture of how our GTM tools connect, and the quality of the data inside them
  • Own what you build end to end, including monitoring, error handling, and the guardrails on anything AI-generated that reaches a restaurant
  • Know our stack, know what exists in the market that we are not yet using, and make the case for what we adopt, replace or retire
  • Set the roadmap and bring a clear, defensible point of view on what gets built first
  • Measure the impact: repetitive hours removed across Sales and CX, territory coverage and data accuracy, booked conversations generated, and speed to lead

Requirements

What We're Looking For

Non-Negotiables

  • 5+ years in GTM engineering, revenue operations, growth or marketing operations, including time owning a function rather than a slice of one
  • Self-directed by default. You can point to problems you identified yourself, decided were worth solving, and drove to completion
  • Strong SQL and working Python or equivalent. You can connect two systems with no native integration
  • AI in production. You have shipped AI-driven workflows that reach real customers, and you can explain your evals, guardrails and human-review step before anything goes out
  • CRM architecture rather than administration. Salesforce or HubSpot, plus modern enrichment and orchestration tooling: Clay, n8n, Make or equivalent
  • Commercial instinct, and a track record of shipping work with teams you do not manage

Strong Preference

  • High-velocity, low-ACV motions. Cycles under 30 days and thousands of accounts per market
  • Restaurant tech, hospitality SaaS, or vertical SaaS
  • Local business or multi-location data
  • Experience building without a large team, in a startup or scale-up environment

Who You Are

  • A builder, not a maintainer. You are energized by an open scope rather than unsettled by it
  • Strategic without being asked. You bring a point of view on what should happen next and you can defend it
  • Focused on leverage. You measure your work by the hours and errors you take out of other people's days

Benefits

Who We Are

Popmenu is a fast-growing, venture-backed SaaS company transforming the restaurant industry. We started with our patented dynamic menu technology, unleashing the power of a restaurant's most important marketing tool, the menu. Since then, we have continued innovating to solve existing and emerging challenges for restaurant operators. We do not just sell software. We partner with restaurants to help them win. Our mission is to empower owners and operators with the technology tools they need to succeed long into the future. We hire exceptionally bright, motivated people who are passionate about helping great restaurants reach their full potential.

Compensation

  • Base: $140,000 to $150,000
  • Annual bonus target: 20% of base
  • Equity included for every employee

Why Popmenu

  • Our first GTM Engineer, with meaningful ownership of the function from day one
  • A direct line to our Chief Business Officer and Co-Founder
  • Full-funnel scope across Sales, Marketing and CX rather than one narrow slice
  • Remote across the US, a product restaurants rely on, and equity for every team member

What We're Serving

  • Remote, United States
  • Genuine Core Values with quarterly peer recognition through our Super Booms
  • Giving Back with company donations to causes chosen by team members
  • Visible Growth and Development in a scaling SaaS company where your impact is seen and rewarded
  • Company Ownership with meaningful equity for every employee
  • Comprehensive Benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and Wagmo Wellness Plan for your pets

jobs.description:
Statistiker:in (m/w/d)

Ab 4.500 € brutto / Monat · Klare Steigerung nach Ergebnissen · Kleines Team, große Verantwortung

Worum es geht

Wir begleiten Mediziner:innen durch ihre Promotion — von Methodik über Auswertung bis zur fertigen Dissertation. Unsere Klient:innen sind keine Studenten, sondern erwachsene Profis, die liefern müssen. Du bist die Person, die dafür sorgt, dass das passiert.

Konkret heißt das: Du übernimmst Projekte von der ersten Methodendiskussion bis zur finalen Abgabe. Du analysierst Daten (R, Python, SPSS, MAXQDA — je nachdem, was das Projekt verlangt), überarbeitest wissenschaftliche Texte, erklärst Doktorand:innen Methoden ruhig und klar, gibst Feedback, hältst Termine ein und triffst Entscheidungen, ohne dass jemand dich an die Hand nehmen muss.

Ehrlich gesagt

Wir sind ein kleines Unternehmen mit hoher Schlagzahl und hoher Effizienz. Wir brauchen sorgfältige, einsatzbereite und belastbare Leute, die methodisch sauber arbeiten, überdurchschnittlich verdienen wollen und in einem wachsenden Unternehmen von Anfang an dabei sein wollen.

Im Gegenzug bekommst du etwas, das ein Konzern nicht bieten kann: Vom ersten Tag an eigene Projekte, direkten Kundenkontakt, sichtbare Wirkung, und einen Aufstieg, der sich an deinen Ergebnissen bemisst und nicht an deiner Betriebszugehörigkeit.

Was du machst

  • Mediziner:innen durch den kompletten Promotionsprozess führen — Methodik, Statistik, Schreiben, Struktur

  • Statistische und qualitative Auswertungen liefern (R, Python, SPSS, MAXQDA)

  • Doktorand:innen Methoden geduldig und klar erklären — schriftlich und im Gespräch

  • Wissenschaftliche Texte überarbeiten, Feedback geben, methodische Sauberkeit sicherstellen

  • Mehrere parallele Projekte koordinieren — Termine, Qualität, Kundenkontakt

  • KI- und Automatisierungstools so einsetzen, dass du schneller und besser wirst als ohne

  • Mit Professor:innen, Lehrstühlen und Forschungsstellen sauber kommunizieren

Was du mitbringst

  • Hochschulabschluss (Bachelor oder Master) in Statistik, Psychologie (empirisch/quantitativ), Sozialwissenschaft (quant), Wirtschaftsmathematik, BWL mit Empirie-Schwerpunkt, Mathematik, Public Health (quantitativ) oder vergleichbar. Eine Promotion ist nicht erforderlich und gibt hier keinen Bonus.

  • Strukturierte, methodische Arbeitsweise. Du planst, bevor du loslegst. Du arbeitest sorgfältig statt hektisch. Du erkennst Inkonsistenzen in Daten oder Texten, die andere überlesen.

  • Aktuelle Statistik-Praxis. Du hast in den letzten 12 Monaten konkret mit R, Python, SPSS oder MAXQDA gearbeitet — nicht nur im Studium.

  • Erfahrung im Erklären von Methoden — als Tutor:in, Nachhilfelehrer:in, Übungsleiter:in, Werkstudent:in im Lehrstuhl-Umfeld oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle. Wer Lernenden schon einmal Statistik ruhig erklärt hat, bringt das wichtigste Soft-Skill mit.

  • Emotionale Stabilität. Wenn ein:e Klient:in panisch wird, bleibst du ruhig. Wenn drei Mandate parallel brennen, sortierst du methodisch, statt dich anstecken zu lassen. Du nimmst Fehler sachlich, nicht persönlich.

  • Eigenverantwortung und Verbindlichkeit. Du strukturierst deinen Tag selbst, hältst Deadlines ein, lieferst zuverlässig — auch wenn niemand drüberguckt.

  • Belastbarkeit in intensiven Phasen — keine Schönwetter-Mentalität.

  • Deutsch auf C2-Niveau — du musst Texte korrigieren und gegenüber Senior-Klient:innen klar, aber respektvoll argumentieren können.

  • Lust auf Privatwirtschaft, nicht auf Uni-Atmosphäre.

Berufserfahrung von Vorteil, aber kein Muss. Wir nehmen auch Berufseinsteiger:innen mit starkem Tutor-Track. Mit 2-5 Jahren Berufserfahrung in datenorientierten Bereichen (Marktforschung, Pharma-Innendienst, Junior Analytics, klinische Studien) bist du im Vorteil.

Was wir bieten

  • Geld: Ab 4.500 € brutto, reale Steigerung in den ersten 6–12 Monaten nach Ergebnissen

  • Aufstieg nach Leistung: Wer liefert, kommt schnell hoch — Zugehörigkeit zählt nicht

  • Echte Verantwortung: Eigene Projekte, eigene Kunden, eigene Entscheidungen — ab Tag 1

  • Profi-Umfeld: MacBook, moderne Tools, KI-Stack — keine Bastellösungen

  • Klare Strukturen: Max. 2–3 Personen pro Büro, keine Konzernpolitik, keine Meetings ohne Zweck

  • Entwicklung: Methodisch, technisch und unternehmerisch — du wächst hier real

Wen wir nicht suchen

Wir suchen keine Akademiker:innen, die in der Forschungsblase bleiben wollen. Keine Theoretiker:innen, die sich in Details verlieren, ohne zu liefern. Keine Leute, die "Work-Life-Balance" auf das Stundenkonto reduzieren. Wer langsam, unzuverlässig oder konfliktscheu ist, wird hier nicht glücklich — und wir auch nicht.

Wir suchen jemanden, der ruhig, methodisch und ergebnisorientiert arbeitet — und dafür entsprechend bezahlt werden will.

Bewerbung

Schick uns Lebenslauf und ein aussagekräftiges und persönliches Anschreiben.

  1. Warum du in eine kleine Firma willst — nicht in einen Konzern oder die Uni.

  2. Was du in den nächsten 12 Monaten konkret erreichen möchtest.

Relevante Arbeiten, Code oder Projektbeispiele gerne dazu.

Unvollständige Bewerbungen sortieren wir aus. Bei passenden Bewerbungen melden wir uns innerhalb von 5 Werktagen.

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

The Executive Assistant to the CEO is one of the most critical roles at Imprint. You will serve as the right hand to our Founder and CEO, ensuring that their time, focus, and energy are directed toward the highest impact priorities across the business. This is not a traditional administrative role. You will operate as a true strategic partner who creates leverage for the CEO by managing complexity, anticipating needs, and keeping the operating rhythm of the company running smoothly behind the scenes.

Imprint is at a pivotal stage of growth. We have over 220 employees, are nearly doubling in revenue year over year, and are preparing to launch several major new brand partnerships. The CEO is deeply involved across product, partnerships, fundraising, board governance, and company culture. This role exists to make sure nothing falls through the cracks and that the CEO can operate at the highest possible level every single day.

You will be based in our New York City office and expected to be in the office when the CEO is in the office, which is most days. This role requires someone who thrives in a fast-paced, high-ownership environment and who genuinely loves the craft of being an exceptional Executive Assistant.

What You'll Do

  • Manage and optimize a complex, fast-moving calendar across multiple time zones, balancing internal meetings, board commitments, investor conversations, partner meetings, and personal time. Own the CEO's schedule entirely and make daily judgment calls about what gets prioritized, rescheduled, or declined.

  • Coordinate all logistics for board meetings, investor meetings, and partner events including preparation of materials, room setup, travel arrangements, attendee communications, and follow-up items. Ensure the CEO walks into every meeting fully prepared and that nothing is left to chance.

  • Serve as a gatekeeper and liaison between the CEO and internal teams, external partners, investors, board members, and other stakeholders.

  • Track and follow up on action items, commitments, and deliverables that come out of meetings and conversations. Maintain a running system that ensures nothing the CEO committed to gets dropped.

  • Help prepare for key company moments including all-hands meetings, leadership offsites, and major announcements by coordinating logistics, gathering materials, and ensuring smooth execution.

  • Support light personal tasks as needed to ensure the CEO can stay focused on the business during high-intensity periods.

  • Proactively identify opportunities to improve how the CEO's office operates. Bring ideas for better systems, tools, and workflows that create more leverage and reduce friction.

What We're Looking For

  • 10+ years of experience as an Executive Assistant, with at least 2 years directly supporting a CEO or Founder at a high-growth technology or fintech company. You have supported an executive through a period of rapid scaling and understand what it takes to keep up with the pace.

jobs.description:
TENGOINTERNET

Fractional Marketing Manager

Part-time contract (1099) • ~10–15 hours/week • Remote (Central Texas preferred) • $3,000–$5,000/month retainer

About TengoInternet

TengoInternet is an employee-owned company that has spent more than two decades designing, building, and managing outdoor WiFi networks for campgrounds, RV resorts, glamping destinations, and marinas. Our customers count on us to keep their guests connected and their operations running — and they stay with us because of trust, relationships, and results. Get Connected.

Why this role exists

Our longtime marketing leader recently moved on, and rather than replace the role one-for-one, we redesigned the function. Strategy is set by our leadership team; automation and specialists handle the heavy systems work. What we need now is a reliable, hands-on marketing generalist to own the marketing execution across our prospect and customer lifecycle — nurturing leads, strengthening customer relationships, supporting expansion and referrals, and ensuring our industry presence translates into measurable business outcomes. This person will also keep our brand present and our busy trade show calendar running smoothly.

One thing to know: Tengo wins through relationships and credibility, not marketing volume. Most of our best customers come from referrals and industry events. Your job is to amplify that — keep us top-of-mind with customers and prospects, make every event count, and make sure no lead falls through the cracks.

What you’ll own

1. Prospect & Customer Nurturing

  • Own the ongoing marketing cadence for active prospects, dormant opportunities, customers, and strategic accounts.
  • Ensure trade-show leads, closed/lost opportunities, early-stage construction projects, and other “not now” prospects enter appropriate nurture programs rather than disappearing from view.
  • Partner with Sales and Customer Success to identify and execute customer expansion campaigns around portfolio growth, network lifecycle/upgrade opportunities, new services, and other relevant Tengo capabilities.
  • Build recurring customer communications that support retention, expansion, referrals, upgrades, and adoption of additional Tengo services.
  • Identify customer wins that can become testimonials, referrals, case studies, reviews, or other trust-building assets.
  • Work with our HubSpot specialist to translate lifecycle needs into automated workflows and sequences.

2. Content & Thought Leadership: emails and blogs

•Write and schedule recurring email campaigns in HubSpot: educational content for existing customers, nurture touches for prospects and dormant leads, and pre/post-event sends.

•Write and schedule our promotional emails and blog posts for posting through our ad partners

•Turn CEO-provided ideas, observations, meeting notes and industry insights into first drafts of CEO Connect and other thought-leadership communications, preserving the CEO's voice and point of view for his final review.

•Publish 1–2 blog posts per month aligned to our SEO/AEO roadmap (we have an audit and keyword direction — you execute against it).

•Turn wins into proof: case studies, testimonials, and review snippets we can reuse across channels.

  • Work efficiently across channels by repurposing strong source content and using AI appropriately for drafting and production.

3. Light social media and website maintenance

•Keep Facebook and LinkedIn active (roughly 1–2 posts/week) by repurposing blog, email, and event content — consistency over volume.

•Promote our presence before, during, and after trade shows; celebrate customer milestones and company news.

•Responding to social comments and reviews on Google, etc

•Periodic content updates to our Wordpress website—You do not need to be a professional web designer.

4. Lead attribution and funnel management

•Own lead-source data quality in HubSpot: every new lead tagged with channel and source (referral, event, web/AI search, advertising, cold outreach) so we know what’s working.

•Produce a simple monthly lead-source and funnel report for the sales and leadership team.

•Own event lead capture end-to-end: badge scans and booth conversations get into HubSpot and enrolled in follow-up sequences within days, not weeks.

  • Own the marketing process for systematically generating customer and partner referrals, including identifying appropriate moments to ask, developing campaigns and communications, coordinating referral incentives where appropriate, and tracking referral results.

5. Conference planning and logistics

•Quarterback our trade show calendar (OHI, KOA, Campground Owners Expo, and the Glamping Show are our keystones): registrations, sponsorship and ad deadlines, booth services, and company profiles.

•Coordinate booth and swag shipping, hotel blocks, and travel deadlines with our internal event support — you run the checklist and the calendar so nothing books late or ships late.

•Run a simple pre-event protocol: staffing confirmed before we commit, meetings booked before we arrive, follow-up ready before we leave.

  • Proactively identify speaking, panel, roundtable, sponsorship and thought-leadership opportunities that position Tengo above the noise of the exhibit hall.
  • Work with leadership and Sales before key events to identify target accounts, relationship introductions and meetings we want to create.

•Deliver a short post-event recap: leads captured, meetings held, cost, and what we’d change.

What success looks like in the first 90 days

•Fall/winter event season (Glamping Show, OHI, KOA, and others) runs on a documented checklist with zero missed deadlines.

•A monthly customer email and a steady social cadence are live and on-brand.

•Every new lead in HubSpot carries a source, and leadership sees a monthly report they trust.

•Event leads are followed up within one week via a repeatable sequence.

What this role is not

•Not a CMO or strategy role — leadership sets direction; you’ll have a seat at our standing marketing meeting and real input, but this is an execution-first engagement.

•Not a HubSpot architecture project — specialist help handles complex automation builds; you need to be fluent, not an architect.

•Not a heavy paid-media role — we run modest industry advertising, not large ad budgets.

•Not a social media content creator role -- we don’t need tons of video production, etc

You’re a fit if you have

•4+ years of B2B marketing experience as a hands-on generalist — ideally supporting a relationship-driven sales team.

•Strong writing chops: you can shift between a practical educational email, a CEO’s voice, and a blog post that reads like a human wrote it.

•Working fluency in HubSpot (email, lists, forms, basic workflows, reporting).

•Real event/trade show operations experience — you’ve owned deadlines, vendors, shipping, and travel logistics before.

•The fractional mindset: self-managing, deadline-driven, comfortable flexing hours up during event season and down in quieter months.

•Comfort using AI tools to draft faster without letting them write on autopilot.

Bonus points: outdoor hospitality / campground / RV industry familiarity; WordPress; Canva or Adobe; Google Ads; SEO/AEO experience.

Engagement details

•Independent contractor (1099) on a monthly retainer of $3,000–$5,000 depending on experience and scope, at roughly 10–15 hours/week.

•Initial 90-day engagement with the intent of a long-term ongoing relationship.

•You’ll work day-to-day with our fractional sales leader and internal event support, with a standing marketing meeting alongside our CEO and sales leader.

jobs.description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for backend engineers to build the core systems behind BJAK's AI Neobank app.

This role is for engineers who can build reliable APIs, workflows and financial product infrastructure that can scale across markets, partners and millions of users.

What You'll Own

  • Build backend services and APIs for onboarding, accounts, payments, cards, transfers, rewards, travel, FX, KYC and risk flows.

  • Design reliable systems that can support real customer transactions, operational workflows and future financial products.

  • Integrate with internal systems, financial partners, payment providers, AI services and third-party platforms.

  • Own backend quality across reliability, security, latency, observability, data integrity and incident handling.

  • Work with product, frontend, mobile and AI teams to launch features quickly and safely.

  • Improve existing systems by simplifying flows, removing manual work and automating repeatable processes.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong backend engineering experience in production systems.

  • Good understanding of APIs, databases, authentication, authorization, queues, jobs, events and integrations.

  • Experience building services used by real customers or internal operations at meaningful scale.

  • Strong debugging, reliability, security and data quality mindset.

  • Able to make practical trade-offs between speed, correctness, scalability and maintainability.

  • Fintech, payments, banking, wallet, KYC, fraud or risk experience is a strong plus, but not required if fundamentals are strong.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who only want isolated backend tasks.

  • People who ignore security, data consistency, monitoring or operational risk.

  • Developers who cannot work with fast-changing product requirements.

  • Candidates who talk about scale but have not handled production systems.

  • People who exaggerate impact without being clear on ownership.


The Bar

We are looking for engineers with real technology career highlights. A strong highlight is not just working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or system.

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Indonesia. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Indonesia.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Technical interview

3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

​​Looking for Philippines-based candidates

Job Role: Graphic Designer and Content Specialist

Compensation range: $2,000 AUD - $3,000 AUD/Monthly

Engagement type:Independent Contractor Agreement

Work Schedule: This role is expected to align with the AU business hours (approx. 9 AM - 5 PM, Monday to Friday) for collaboration, but as a contractor, you’ll have flexibility in how you manage your time.

Who We Are: At Hunt St, we help Australian companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines. For this role, you will be engaged directly by the client as an independent contractor. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote so you'll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is: Our client offers the opportunity to work directly with the founder across three growing Australian brands spanning mortgage lending, skincare, and daily multivitamin supplements. With substantial real-world ad spend already in market and multiple brands requiring fresh creative, the business is building out its content capabilities with above-market pay for the right creative talent.

Role Overview: Our client is looking for an experienced Graphic Designer & Content Specialist who can work directly with the founder across multiple Australian brands spanning mortgage lending, skincare, and daily multivitamin supplements.

This is not a role for someone who needs to be trained from the ground up. We’re looking for a creative operator who can take an idea, turn it into high-quality content, use AI to accelerate production, and understand what makes digital advertising perform.

What You’ll Do

  • Create high-quality static and video creative for Meta ads, email marketing, and social media across multiple brands.
  • Produce mortgage advertising focused on non-bank specialty lending and debt consolidation.
  • Turn raw skincare footage into polished 15–20 second video ads, alongside static creative.
  • Create content for a growing daily multivitamin supplement brand.
  • Develop multiple creative variations from winning concepts, hooks, formats, and visual angles.
  • Review creative performance and use insights such as hook/hold rate, CTR and other Meta Ads Manager data to inform new iterations.
  • Work from existing winners and rapidly produce new variants rather than waiting for detailed briefs.
  • Use AI throughout the creative workflow, including AI image generation, AI video, voiceover, editing, enhancement and upscaling.
  • Maintain brand consistency across multiple businesses while adapting creative to different audiences and offers.
  • Support email creative for a database of 10,000+ HubSpot contacts.
  • Help build out the brands’ social content where required, without allowing social management to take priority over paid creative production.

Requirements

AI & Creative Technology — Required

AI is a core requirement of this role, not a nice-to-have. You should have hands-on experience using tools such as:

  • AI Image: Midjourney, Adobe Firefly, Nano Banana or equivalent
  • AI Video: Veo, Sora, Runway or equivalent
  • AI Voice: ElevenLabs or equivalent
  • Upscaling/Enhancement: Topaz or equivalent
  • Other AI tools that improve creative production speed and quality

You should be able to explain how you use AI as part of your actual production workflow, not simply demonstrate that you have experimented with AI tools.

Required Software

Professional experience with:

  • Adobe Premiere Pro
  • Adobe After Effects or CapCut for high-volume production
  • Adobe Photoshop
  • Adobe Illustrator
  • Figma
  • Canva — genuine requirement

Experience working with Canva brand kits is particularly important. This role requires someone comfortable moving between professional Adobe workflows and fast, practical Canva production.

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong commercial graphic design and video editing experience.
  • Experience creating live digital advertising creative, not just portfolio pieces.
  • Strong understanding of what makes an ad visually compelling and attention-grabbing.
  • Ability to take a winning creative and quickly develop multiple meaningful variations.
  • Comfortable working with performance data and using it to improve creative output.
  • Strong understanding of short-form video, hooks, pacing and retention.
  • Highly proficient across the required design, video and AI tools.
  • Able to work independently, move quickly, and produce finished work without extensive hand-holding.
  • Strong attention to brand consistency while being willing to test new creative directions.

Work Arrangement & Expectations:

This is a remote role that will be set up as an independent contractor engagement.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:

  • Disclose any existing ongoing roles or client work
  • Reflect this engagement on their LinkedIn profile (clearly marked as “Independent Contractor”)

You’ll take ownership of the development lifecycle—from understanding the business problem and shaping the backlog, to designing, building, deploying, and supporting solutions across the Microsoft Power Platform.

jobs.description:
Category: Government & Public Sector

Location:


PLEASE NOTE:
  • It is a 100% remote position.
DESCRIPTION OF PROJECT:
The Client is seeking one full-time resource to provide Quality Assurance (QA) Automation Programmer/Developer experience to provide technical leadership for automation efforts supporting the Minnesota Eligibility Technology System (METS)/SMRT DevOps team. QA has multiple efforts in progress of automating the QA Regression suite and needs a resource to assist successful completion of work, while documenting processes and procedures for ongoing maintenance and execution. Areas include, but are not limited to, METS, and other DHS and ISDS initiatives that demands support. In addition to this effort, once initial development is complete, make ongoing updates and new test case automation as well as improve overall efficiency of the automation.
At a high level, the resource will provide senior-level technical leadership for automation architecture, framework design, and automation best practices while supporting ongoing modernization initiatives and continuous delivery efforts.
TASKS:
  • Design, develop, maintain, and modernize the enterprise automation framework supporting the State's integrated healthcare eligibility system, ensuring long-term maintainability, scalability, sustainability, and reuse across multiple modernization initiatives.
  • Provide technical leadership for automation architecture, framework design, coding standards, and automation best practices within the DevOps team.
  • Evaluate and modernize existing automation frameworks to improve maintainability, scalability, reliability, and execution efficiency.
  • Collaborate with developers, business analysts, DevOps engineers, and QA staff to define automation strategies, reusable test assets, and technical solutions.
  • Design, execute, and maintain functional, system integration, API, and regression automation suites supporting statewide healthcare eligibility systems.
  • Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines and support automated execution throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Mentor automation engineers through code reviews, technical coaching, framework guidance, and knowledge transfer.
  • Develop SQL queries and perform database validation to support automated testing and troubleshoot complex application issues.
  • Participate in Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, backlog refinement, defect triage, and technical design discussions while providing automation leadership.
  • Research, evaluate, and recommend new automation tools, technologies, and framework enhancements that improve software quality and long-term maintainability.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES & ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
  • Test Automation & Framework Development
  • Design, build, execute, and maintain scalable automated test scripts and testing frameworks for web, mobile, and API applications.
  • Perform automated functional, regression, integration, performance, and end-to-end (E2E) testing to ensure software meets specifications.
  • Integrate automated test execution into Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines to enable continuous quality feedback.
  • Maintain and optimize existing automated test suites to accommodate changing software features and reduce execution time.
  • Client Liaison & Stakeholder Management
  • Act as a primary liaison for client representatives, business analysts, and product owners regarding quality assurance, testing progress, and release readiness.
  • Translate business requirements and acceptance criteria into clear, executable automated test cases and scenarios.
  • Present automated test results, coverage metrics, and defect trends to client stakeholders in clear, actionable briefings.
  • Lead and facilitate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) sessions with client end-users, guiding them through system validation.
  • Defect Tracking, Quality Control & Analysis
  • Identify, log, track, and prioritize software defects and edge-case anomalies using standard defect management systems.
  • Perform root-cause analysis on test failures and collaborate directly with software engineering teams to accelerate issue remediation.
  • Author detailed test execution reports, quality summary dashboards, and traceability matrices ensuring complete coverage of system requirements.
  • Agile Collaboration & Team Support
  • Participate actively in Agile/Scrum ceremonies, including sprint planning, backlog grooming, daily stand-ups, and sprint reviews.
  • Work cross-functionally with system architects, developers, UI/UX designers, and project managers throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC).
  • Recommend process improvements and continuous quality enhancements to elevate software testing standards

Requirements

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Seven (7) years’ experience designing, developing, and executing automated test solutions for large-scale enterprise applications.
  • Five (5) years’ experience developing automation frameworks using Java and Selenium or comparable automation technologies.
  • Five (5) years’ experience designing, developing, or significantly enhancing automation frameworks using object-oriented design principles and reusable framework architecture.
  • Three (3) years’ experience integrating automated testing into Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines using tools such as Jenkins.
  • Five (5) years’ experience writing SQL queries and performing database validation in support of automated testing.

TECHNICAL TOOLS & AUTOMATION:
  • Automation Tools & Frameworks: Command of core automation tools such as Selenium WebDriver, Playwright, Cypress, Appium, or Playwright.
  • API Testing: Proficient in automated API testing using tools like Postman, RestAssured, or SoapUI.
  • Programming / Scripting: Proficient in at least one object-oriented or scripting language used in automation (e.g., Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, or C#).
  • Defect & Backlog Management: Hands-on experience with Atlassian Jira, Azure DevOps (ADO), or Quality Center/ALM.
  • CI/CD Integration: Working knowledge of integrating automated tests into build/deployment pipelines using Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Azure Pipelines.
  • Methodologies: Strong practical knowledge of Agile (Scrum/Kanban) and Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) / Test-Driven Development (TDD) using frameworks like Cucumber or Behave.

DESIRED SKILLS:
  • Experience serving as an Automation Architect, Principal QA Automation Engineer, Automation Framework Lead, or Senior Automation Consultant.

jobs.description:
🌍 Join Triptease — Where Travel Tech Meets Impact

At Triptease, we’re building technology that helps hotels thrive in a digital world dominated by Online Travel Agents. Our products empower hotels to increase direct bookings, regain profitability, and build closer relationships with their guests.

Already helping generate over £1 billion in direct revenue annually, we’re scaling fast across 100+ countries with offices in London, New York, Barcelona, and Singapore. It’s a fantastic time to join us as we grow our impact and expand our engineering teams.

We’re a team that values authenticity, ownership, inclusion, and delivering meaningful work — together.

🚀 About the Role

We’re looking for a Mid Level Software Engineer who thrives in solving complex problems, working closely with others, and experimenting with new technologies. You will have excellent experience with backend projects and have also worked as a full stack engineer. You’ll help us craft accessible user experiences, design scalable systems, and explore how AI and automation can make our platform smarter and more impactful for hoteliers worldwide.

🐒 About the Tamarin Squad

Tamarin looks after Triptease’s core off-site marketing channels: Metasearch, Paid Search and Retargeting. Our mission is to empower hotels with control over these channels, giving them the tools to shape strategy, reach their most valuable guests and drive direct bookings.

We’re a collaborative team working mainly in TypeScript (Node.js and React) with Google Cloud Run, Kubernetes, Terraform and BigQuery. Day to day we build backend services, integrations with platforms like the Google Ads API, and features within Campaign Manager that give hoteliers both strategic control and tactical flexibility.

Our main challenges include unifying channels into a connected system, balancing automation with customer control, and staying ahead of the fast-changing Google ecosystem. We value continuous learning, autonomy and product thinking; every engineer contributes ideas and helps shape the squad’s direction, not just the code.

🛠️ Our Tech Stack

  • Languages: Primarily TypeScript, with some Kotlin and Python
  • Backend: Node.js, experimenting with modern alternatives like Bun
  • Frontend: React for admin tools and reporting (minimal UI work)
  • Infrastructure: Google Cloud Run, Kubernetes, Terraform
  • Data: BigQuery, PostgreSQL, MySQL
  • Integrations: Google Ads API, various metasearch and advertising platforms

🧩 Your Day-to-Day

You’ll be part of a small, empowered squad responsible for building, growing, and maintaining key parts of the Triptease stack. While the work spans both frontend and backend, there’s a strong lean toward backend systems.

On a typical day, you’ll:

  • Pair program with teammates for the majority of your coding time.
  • Take part in daily standups, weekly planning sessions, and frequent retros to continuously improve how we work.
  • Collaborate openly with colleagues — we value honest discussion and make sure everyone’s voice is heard.
  • Contribute to a team that owns its strategy end-to-end, deciding together what actions to take to succeed.
  • Practice trunk-based development and continuous delivery, shipping small, incremental changes to production.

Requirements

✅ What You’ll Bring

  • XP Engineering Practices: Comfortable with pair programming most of the day, and see test-driven development (TDD) as integral to building reliable systems. You use tests to drive design, embrace refactoring as part of everyday coding, and value small, incremental code and test cycles.
  • Backend and Full-Stack Experience: Strong backend experience in TypeScript with additional frontend skills for admin UIs. Solid skills across the full stack, from client-side to server-side development.
  • Cloud-Native Experience: Practical experience building deployment pipelines and continuous delivery on cloud platforms. Familiarity with Google Cloud Platform, Docker, Kubernetes, and Terraform.
  • Data Systems and Analytics: Experience with PostgreSQL, MySQL, and BigQuery. Passion for working with data to power real-time analytics, A/B testing, and monitoring with tools like DataDog.
  • Systems Thinking: Experience designing and building distributed, high-availability, high-throughput systems while maintaining modularity, functionality, maintainability, and data consistency. Solid understanding of HTTP and how the internet works.
  • Code Quality: You write obvious, concise code that rarely needs comments and always leave the codebase better than you found it.
  • Product Mindset and Collaboration: Customer-centric approach, working closely with product managers to ensure technical solutions deliver value. You contribute ideas and strategy, not just code, and thrive in collaborative environments that drive squad momentum.
  • Values Alignment: Commitment to continuous learning, autonomy, psychological safety, and developing your craft.

⭐ Bonus Points

  • Experience with online advertising or ad tech products.
  • Familiarity with the Google Ads API.
  • gRPC experience (we maintain a TypeScript Google Ads API library).
  • You have an entrepreneurial streak, with examples of how you identified opportunities and delivered them.
  • Experience in cross-functional teams practising XP (Extreme Programming) and Kanban techniques.
  • Familiarity with multiple programming languages and the ability to bring insights and practices across ecosystems.

Benefits

🧡 Perks & Benefits

We’re a remote-first Product & Engineering team, working across the UK and Europe (London +/- 1h GMT). You can work from our London office, from home, or a mix of both. Whatever suits you best. We meet regularly in person for team and company events (next stop: Madrid!).

What we offer:

Our start-up culture (more on this below) means everyone's contribution really matters. It's an inclusive, outcome-orientated and fun place to work.

  • We’re committed to your career development, most of our staff have seen considerable learning and progression. There is space to take dedicated learning time out each week to further improve your craft. Triptease will also fund training and conferences if you tell us why we should.
  • We like to offer all our employees a stake in our success which is why we offer share options.
  • Paid vacation (increasing with tenure)
  • Work from anywhere: 4 weeks abroad annually (within a ±3 hour time zone)
  • Monthly wellness budget – use it for gym, therapy, massages, or whatever keeps you at your best
  • Yearly learning allowance – invest in your growth!
  • Enhanced maternity & paternity leave
  • 10 "Discovery Days" per year to explore innovative ideas together with colleagues from around the business
  • Fun events for Tripteasers - the entire company is travelling to Madrid this September for a global retreat.
  • Whatever equipment helps you get your job done.

Something important to you that's not on this list? Talk to us!

Our Operating Model & Culture

  • In Product-Engineering, we hire people we trust, and then trust them to make their own choices on how they want to work, and how they want to reach a goal. This sounds simple but it requires a lot of investment in the right company culture. Our team is made up of autonomous squads who decide what they work on, how they work and within them have all the skills they need to complete their mission. That means we have no centralised teams (Ops, QA etc).
  • We think that we are doing a good thing for hotels and guests and believe in our mission! We are working on a highly scaled platform that hotels use to build direct relationships with their customers and cut out middlemen. In terms of scale, our software operates on over 10k hotels and collects ~30M guest events a day, and growing. That's a big opportunity to positively impact a lot of people.
  • We engage with our customers to validate assumptions and test new features. We like to go crazy deep on the problem. 'Start with the problem' is one of our three core principles, and beyond tools like FullStory, Intercom and Analytics that help us learn about users, each squad has friends in CS and Sales and even hoteliers themselves to help build that knowledge. Hotel visits and travel research budgets are also a big plus.
  • We care deeply about diversity and inclusion. We have a dedicated D&I squad who meet regularly to work on and propose actions to improve D&I within the team and wider biz. Outside of hiring activities, we work hard to foster an environment of psychological safety. We truly value collaboration and are invested in maintaining a team that encourages everyone to contribute.
  • We optimise for learning. We regularly provide each other with feedback and reflect on the ways we work. We use Notion to bring efficient transparency and create a home for everything we do. We have initiatives like 'Discovery Days', 'Field Trips' and 'Product Management Dojos' to bring new people together and create more learning and development opportunities.
  • We celebrate our progress. At the end of each week, we join the rest of the company to showcase what we’ve accomplished and share our pride in the work we have done with our colleagues.

—

We welcome applications from diverse and non-traditional backgrounds. Applicants will not be discriminated against on the basis of any protected characteristic(s) in terms of the Equality Act (2010).

jobs.description:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it ourselves at world scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care (the AI doctor), starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform currently automates 95% of the administrative work required for us to deliver direct patient care. We also recently became the first company ever to receive regulatory authorization to let AI prescribe psychiatric medications, allowing us to not only collapse health care’s admin costs but also its clinical labor costs—shifting this industry’s economics from humans to tokens.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us produce tens of thousands of total visits in just 2 years, all while holding ops costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention. While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision? A 10X better patient experience that’s higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable than ever before. And a 10X better clinician experience that frees our providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by doctors and AI working together.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Full-Time

  • Role Type: Lifecycle Marketing / CRM / AI-Native Patient Engagement / Retention / Growth

  • Ideal Experience Level: 6+ years, including 3+ years owning lifecycle, CRM, retention, or owned-channel growth

  • Location: In-Person in San Francisco, CA

  • US Visa Sponsorship: Yes

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring an AI Lifecycle Product and Marketing Leader to build the AI-native patient communication engine that helps people start care, stay in care, come back when they lapse, and feel personally supported across months and years of treatment.

This is not a typical lifecycle marketing job. We are not looking for someone to manage a static email calendar, build a few drip campaigns, and optimize subject lines. Legion has rich patient data, production AI, clinical workflows, scheduling events, insurance data, intake behavior, appointment history, medication renewal patterns, and care operations all inside one vertically integrated system. That means we can build something far more powerful: a personalized, proactive communication engine that knows where each patient is in their journey and automatically helps move them to the next right step.

You will build the system that makes Legion feel impossibly responsive. A patient who stalls in intake should get the right nudge. A patient who books but does not complete prep should get the right reminder. A patient at risk of missing follow-up should be guided before they lapse. A patient due for renewal should understand what to do next. A patient who churned should receive a thoughtful, relevant path back. Over time, the engine should become more intelligent, more personalized, and more autonomous.

The right person combines the lifecycle rigor of DoorDash, Instacart, Airbnb, or Sephora; the patient-journey discipline of Hims, Thirty Madison, Headway, or Talkiatry; the retention instincts of Noom, Peloton, WHOOP, or Duolingo; and the AI-native curiosity required to build communication systems that can generate, personalize, test, and improve patient journeys at scale.

This is a founding systems-builder role. You should be comfortable designing lifecycle strategy, mapping patient states, writing copy, building CRM logic, creating segments, using AI tools, QAing flows, debugging event data, launching experiments, and partnering with product, engineering, data, ops, and clinical teams to create an engine that increasingly works on its own.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Build Legion’s AI-native lifecycle engine across activation, booking, visit completion, follow-up adherence, medication renewal support, retention, reactivation, and winback.

  • Design the patient communication system across email, SMS, push, in-app, transactional reminders, AI-assisted outreach, and future owned channels.

  • Map the full patient journey into clear lifecycle states, triggers, audiences, suppressions, escalation rules, personalization rules, and next-best-action logic.

  • Use Legion’s patient data to create highly personalized journeys based on intake status, appointment behavior, insurance status, treatment stage, follow-up cadence, renewal needs, engagement, risk of lapse, and communication preferences.

  • Partner with product, engineering, and data to instrument the events, properties, data models, and workflows needed for intelligent lifecycle automation.

  • Build AI-assisted communication workflows that can draft, personalize, route, test, and optimize messages while staying within approved clinical, compliance, and brand guardrails.

  • Create proactive flows for abandoned intake, incomplete booking, pre-visit preparation, appointment reminders, no-show prevention, post-visit follow-up, refill and renewal nudges, reactivation, churn recovery, and long-term engagement.

  • Build segmentation and personalization systems that can support thousands of patient-specific journeys instead of one-size-fits-all campaigns.

  • Partner with clinical operations to ensure every message reflects real care workflows, scheduling capacity, prescribing boundaries, refill policies, escalation paths, and patient support processes.

  • Own lifecycle experimentation across A/B tests, holdouts, incrementality tests, send-time tests, cadence tests, channel-mix tests, AI-personalization tests, and journey-level optimization.

  • Improve core funnel and retention metrics, including intake completion, booking conversion, visit completion, no-show rate, follow-up adherence, reactivation rate, churn, LTV, and patient satisfaction.

  • Build the QA, approval, deliverability, consent, and compliance processes required for high-volume, AI-assisted healthcare communication.

  • Ensure HIPAA, TCPA, CAN-SPAM, consent management, PHI handling, opt-outs, quiet hours, clinical accuracy, and patient trust are treated as product requirements.

  • Create lifecycle dashboards and weekly reporting that show where patients are getting stuck, which journeys are working, and where AI or automation can remove manual work.

  • Evaluate and operate tools such as Braze, Iterable, , HubSpot, Klaviyo, Twilio, SendGrid, PostHog, Hightouch, Segment, RudderStack, Census, OpenAI, Claude, internal AI agents, or similar.

  • Build repeatable lifecycle playbooks that can scale across states, payers, patient segments, care pathways, and future service lines.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Build a lifecycle engine that feels less like marketing automation and more like an intelligent patient guidance system.

  • Turn Legion’s data into personalized, proactive communication that helps patients take the right next action.

  • Meaningfully improve intake completion, booking conversion, kept visits, follow-up adherence, renewal completion, reactivation, and retention.

  • Reduce manual ops work by automating the right nudges, reminders, escalations, and follow-ups before patients fall through the cracks.

  • Make patients feel guided, cared for, and understood, not blasted by generic campaigns.

  • Build event-triggered journeys that move real patient behavior instead of static campaign calendars that sit inside a CRM tool.

  • Create AI-assisted workflows that are useful, accurate, safe, and compliant.

  • Build a testing culture where lifecycle performance improves every week.

  • Maintain extremely high QA standards so messages are accurate, well-timed, correctly personalized, and safe.

  • Help Legion understand which patients are stuck, likely to lapse, ready to return, due for follow-up, or likely to need additional support before the problem becomes manual.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 6+ years in lifecycle marketing, CRM, retention, engagement, growth marketing, patient engagement, consumer communications, or owned-channel marketing.

  • 3+ years directly owning lifecycle programs across email, SMS, push, in-app, transactional messaging, or direct mail.

  • Strong preference for experience in consumer healthcare, marketplaces, subscriptions, mobile apps, fintech, consumer services, e-commerce, or other high-volume consumer businesses.

  • Experience building event-triggered journeys, segmentation systems, personalization logic, suppression rules, send calendars, experimentation roadmaps, and lifecycle reporting.

  • Hands-on fluency with CRM / marketing automation platforms such as Braze, Iterable, , Klaviyo, HubSpot, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, or similar.

  • Strong AI-native operating ability. You should be excited to use LLMs, agents, data, and automation to generate better patient journeys, not just make existing workflows slightly faster.

  • Strong analytical judgment: funnel analysis, cohort analysis, retention curves, A/B tests, holdouts, incrementality, attribution, LTV, churn, and reactivation.

  • Comfort working with data and technical teams. You do not need to be an engineer, but you should understand events, properties, audiences, data quality, QA, and basic SQL or SQL-adjacent analysis.

  • Excellent patient-facing writing judgment. You can make a message clear, warm, action-oriented, personalized, and clinically careful without sounding robotic or promotional.

  • Strong product sense. You understand that lifecycle is not just marketing; it is part of the patient experience, product experience, and operations system.

  • Strong operational rigor around QA, deliverability, consent, localization, link checking, dynamic content, approvals, and launch readiness.

  • Healthcare judgment. You understand that messages about psychiatric care, medication, insurance, no-shows, refills, and follow-up must be handled with real care.

  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with product, engineering, data, clinical operations, customer support, compliance, legal, design, and growth.

  • Low ego, high ownership, and startup intensity. You can define the strategy on Monday, build the segment Tuesday, write the copy Wednesday, QA the flow Thursday, and read the results Friday.

  • Bonus: experience with HIPAA, TCPA, PHI handling, patient engagement, appointment reminders, medication adherence, healthcare CRM, telehealth, LLMs, AI agents, or regulated consumer products.

💰 Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $140,000 – $260,000, based on experience

  • Early-Stage Equity: Competitive

  • Health Insurance: Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Additional Perks: In-person retreats, meal stipends, lifecycle/CRM tooling budget, learning stipend, AI tooling budget

  • Time Off: Flexible, unlimited vacation policy

  • Work Hours: Flexible, with responsiveness around high-impact launches or patient communication issues

  • Work Setup: In-Person in San Francisco, CA

  • Impact: Build the AI-native communication system that helps patients access and stay in high-quality psychiatric care.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Own lifecycle strategy, CRM infrastructure, patient journeys, AI-assisted personalization, experimentation, reporting, and retention systems end-to-end.

  • Growth Opportunities: As Legion scales, this role can grow into Head of Lifecycle, Head of CRM, Head of Patient Engagement, or a broader growth leadership role.

📝 How to Apply and Hiring Process

  • Overview of our hiring process:

    1. Resume + Application Screen

    2. Founder Interview

    3. Lifecycle + AI Systems Deep Dive

    4. Professional Reference Checks

  • Estimated time-to-hire: 2 weeks

  • Start date: ASAP

  • Hiring manager: Arthur MacWaters

Legion is hiring a Insurance Directory Growth and Operations Lead to turn insurance-payer directories into a measurable, scalable patient-acquisition channel. Payer member portals are among the highest-intent places patients look for in-network psychiatric care, yet inaccurate or low-visibility listings create silent failure points: patients cannot find Legion, see the wrong information, or reach a phone-only dead end.

You will own the full directory funnel: authoritative provider data → payer publication → member-side search visibility → click or call to action → eligibility → scheduling → completed first visit. You will be accountable for both operational accuracy and business outcomes, including directory-sourced intakes, booked visits, conversion, and incremental revenue.

This is a hands-on operator role. You should be comfortable auditing large rosters, working inside payer portals, calling and emailing network-operations teams, reconciling CAQH and NPPES data, investigating edge cases, maintaining airtight change logs, creating UTM links, setting up recurring QA, and partnering with Growth and Engineering to route patients into a touchless onboarding experience.

  • Reconcile the source of truth against NPPES, CAQH, credentialing rosters, payer portals, third-party aggregators, and internal provider and contracting systems; define source precedence for every field so discrepancies are resolved consistently.

  • Create a complete baseline inventory and risk-ranked remediation backlog, prioritizing missing providers, inactive or departed providers, wrong locations, missing telehealth indicators, incorrect specialties, duplicate records, broken links, phone-only calls to action, and high-volume payer opportunities.

  • Audit each directory as a patient would: search by ZIP code, state, plan, specialty, telehealth, availability, and accepting-new-patients filters; confirm Legion appears in the expected results and that every profile is accurate, complete, and actionable.

  • Verify that telehealth filters, virtual-visit tags, map pins, specialty mappings, language fields, appointment availability, and accepting-new-patients indicators behave correctly across desktop and mobile directory experiences where available.

  • Submit corrections through the right payer workflow—portal, roster file, API, secure email, ticket, or escalation—and track submission date, confirmation number, payer owner, promised service level, follow-up date, publication date, and member-side verification. A fix is not complete until it is live and independently rechecked.

  • Standardize naming conventions, address formatting, phone numbers, credentials, taxonomy and specialty mappings, group affiliations, telehealth designations, and URL structure; build validation rules and an explicit exception log.

  • Partner with payer directory and network-operations teams to improve Legion’s legitimate search prominence through accurate category mapping, telepsychiatry and virtual-care terminology, featured or virtual-visit badges, complete profile fields, and correct filter eligibility.

  • Replace phone-only or generic calls to action with direct Legion landing pages, self-scheduling links, or SMS short codes wherever payer rules and directory capabilities allow.

  • Create and govern unique UTM-tagged links by payer, network, directory, state, and placement; maintain a durable naming convention, redirect ownership, destination QA, and documentation so attribution survives future updates.

  • Partner with Growth and Engineering to build payer- and state-aware landing experiences, align insurance and availability messaging, reduce intake abandonment, and A/B-test calls to action, trust signals, scheduling flows, and page content.

  • Instrument and validate the directory funnel in PostHog or equivalent analytics from directory referral through eligibility, intake, scheduling, completed first visit, retention, and reactivation; maintain event definitions and investigate attribution gaps.

  • Build weekly reporting that covers inventory completeness, percentage of error-free listings, search-visibility coverage, corrections opened and closed, aging by payer, clicks, intakes, scheduled visits, completed visits, conversion rates, and attributable revenue.

  • Quantify the incremental patient volume and revenue unlocked by each material directory fix; maintain an opportunity model that ranks the backlog by expected impact, confidence, effort, and time to resolution.

  • Establish monthly sweeps and lightweight automated monitoring that detect payer regressions, roster drift, broken URLs, status changes, duplicate records, and unexpected search-result changes before they cost patients or revenue.

  • Integrate provider launches, departures, license changes, new payer contracts, new states, address changes, taxonomy updates, and scheduling changes into a documented change-management workflow with clear owners and service levels.

  • Create payer contact maps, escalation paths, reusable outreach templates, roster-submission checklists, evidence standards, SOPs, and a decision log so the operating system is auditable, repeatable, and transferable.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Deliver a comprehensive, evidence-backed directory inventory within the first 30 days, with every contracted payer and active provider accounted for and no critical listing left without an owner or next action.

  • Reach and maintain at least 98% error-free coverage across high-priority member-facing listings, with critical errors escalated immediately and verified after publication.

  • Ensure high-priority contracted payer searches reliably return the correct Legion providers for relevant psychiatry, telepsychiatry, virtual-care, state, specialty, and accepting-new-patients queries.

  • Turn corrections into durable fixes, not one-time submissions: every closed item has member-side evidence, a verified source record, and a recurring control that reduces the chance of regression.

  • Make directory attribution trustworthy enough to follow source → intake → scheduled visit → completed visit, with clear handling for direct, phone, SMS, redirect, and unattributed traffic.

  • Increase directory-sourced eligibility starts, intakes, scheduled visits, and completed first visits—not just the number of profiles updated or tickets submitted.

  • Reduce time to detect, submit, escalate, and verify directory corrections, and make payer-specific bottlenecks visible before they stall the program.

  • Build monthly sweeps and data-sync workflows that keep manual work near zero without sacrificing field-level accuracy or human verification of member-facing results.

  • Reconcile operational reporting to the underlying roster, payer evidence, and analytics data so leadership can trust every metric and revenue estimate.

  • Identify systemic payer or data-pipeline failures, bring the right internal and external owners together, and drive the issue through to a durable resolution.

  • Move fast without using misleading listings, unsupported specialties, inaccurate availability, spammy tactics, or privacy and compliance shortcuts.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 2+ years in provider-data management, payer or network operations, credentialing, revenue-cycle operations, healthcare data quality, growth operations, or a closely related role.

  • Direct experience updating payer directories, provider-finder tools, or network rosters through platforms such as Availity, CAQH, HealthSmart, payer-specific portals, delegated roster workflows, or third-party directory vendors.

  • Strong working knowledge of Type 1 and Type 2 NPIs, NPPES, CAQH ProView, taxonomy codes, specialties, group affiliations, service locations, telehealth designations, accepting-new-patients status, and network participation.

  • Experience diagnosing discrepancies across multiple systems, determining the authoritative source, documenting the root cause, and verifying the member-facing correction after publication.

  • Advanced comfort with Google Sheets or Excel, including large CSVs, XLOOKUP or VLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, pivot tables, data validation, deduplication, conditional formatting, normalization, and reconciliation.

  • Comfort with lightweight SQL, APIs, JSON or XML, SFTP roster files, scripts, or no-code automation; you do not need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to remove repetitive work.

  • Experience with UTM conventions, redirect QA, PostHog or comparable product analytics, funnel reporting, and conversion-rate measurement.

  • Ability to operate across portals, spreadsheets, email, phone, ticketing systems, and ambiguous payer processes while maintaining precise evidence and follow-up discipline.

  • Strong written and verbal communication. You can write a clean escalation, ask a payer representative for the exact file or field definition needed, and explain the patient and revenue impact of an unresolved issue.

  • Excellent quality-control instincts. You notice one transposed digit, inconsistent taxonomy mapping, outdated address, missing virtual-care tag, or suspicious duplicate—and you investigate until the record is correct.

  • Sound healthcare and privacy judgment. You can work with provider and network data while respecting access controls, minimum-necessary practices, payer rules, and Legion’s compliance requirements.

  • Low ego, high urgency, and end-to-end ownership. You measure success in accurate live listings and completed visits, not activity, submitted forms, or closed spreadsheets.

  • Bonus: Deep familiarity with the Texas payer landscape, multi-state telehealth networks, provider roster standards, directory APIs, delegated credentialing, or provider-data governance at scale.

💰 Compensation & Benefits

  • Hourly Rate: Competitive and based on experience

  • Performance Bonus: Additional compensation tied to strong outcomes such as verified listing accuracy, correction cycle time, directory-sourced booked visits, and measurable revenue impact

  • Contract Structure: Independent contractor (1099)

  • Time Commitment: Approximately 20–40 hours/week

  • Initial Term: 3-month project, renewable based on results and business needs

  • Work Hours: Flexible, with planned overlap for U.S. payer and internal-team coordination

  • Work Setup: Remote

  • Tools: PostHog, analytics dashboards, Google Sheets or Airtable, payer portals, CAQH, NPPES, roster files, APIs, and automation tools

  • Impact: Every accurate, discoverable listing helps a patient find in-network psychiatric care faster and turns an invisible operations fix into measurable clinical and business value.

  • Growth Opportunities: As the program scales, this engagement can expand into broader provider-data governance, payer operations, credentialing systems, or growth-operations ownership.

📝 How to Apply and Hiring Process

  • Apply through the application form on this page.

  • Application materials: Please include your resume and a short note describing the payer portals or provider-directory workflows you have personally owned, plus one example of a discrepancy you took from discovery through verified resolution.

  • Overview of our hiring process:

    • Resume + Application Screen

    • Operations / Founder Interview

    • Provider-Directory Audit + Data Quality Work Sample

    • Final Interview + Professional Reference Checks

  • Estimated time-to-hire: 2 weeks

  • Start date: ASAP

  • Hiring manager: Yash Patel, CEO

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.
